title: UACP: Uncertainty-Aware Channel Prediction in MIMO Networks.
abstract: The key issue with existing compression strategies for multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) channel state information (CSI) feedback is that they rely on strong assumptions about channel statistics. Ultimately this may lead to suboptimal CSI compression and, in turn, inaccurate MIMO precoding in case of model uncertainty and/or model misspecification. In this paper, we propose UACP, the first uncertainty-aware CSI prediction and compression strategy for MIMO systems. UACP is rooted in imprecise probability theory and aims at dynamically selecting the lowest number of subcarriers for channel reporting to guarantee a low CSI prediction error at the transmitter for accurate precoding. UACP uses evidential regression to obtain an estimate of the CSI prediction error in addition to the prediction itself. The key intuition is that such an error is linked with epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty of the prediction process. These two components are effectively disentangled by UACP and used as a proxy to decide the compression level, i.e., the number of subcarriers to be fed back. The results show that UACP reduces feedback overhead by 92.7% and improves throughput by 21.3% relative to Wi-Fi (Ng=4), while incurring only a 0.33% increase in error vector magnitude (EVM). UACP falls back to full feedback and improves bit error rate (BER) by 6.3% under distribution shift.

title: Semantic Multiplexing.
abstract: Mobile devices require the parallel execution of several processing tasks at the edge to reduce their computing load. However, existing communication systems only support parallel transmissions at the bit level. In this paper, we introduce the new concept of Semantic Multiplexing, which shifts stream multiplexing from bits to tasks. By merging multiple task inputs into a single semantic representation, Semantic Multiplexing can multiplex more tasks than the number of physical streams by adding a (semantic) degree of freedom to the communication system. Semantic Multiplexing has been prototyped in an experimental testbed with a Jetson Orin Nano and millimeter-wave software-defined radios. Both image classification (vision) and sentiment analysis tasks (language) have been considered to evaluate Semantic Multiplexing against state-of-the-art baselines. Our experiments indicate that Semantic Multiplexing reduces latency, energy consumption, and communication load by up to 8×, 25×, and 54×, respectively, compared to existing baselines while maintaining comparable performance. For example, image classification accuracy drops only by less than 4% when increasing from 2 to 8 the number of tasks multiplexed over a 4×4 channel. The complete software codebase and the collected datasets are publicly shared for reproducibility1. A video demonstration of Semantic Multiplexing is also available2.

title: Experimental Analysis of Receiver Design for Near-Field Coordinated Beamforming.
abstract: Next-generation wireless networks are envisioned to operate in sub-THz bands to enable increased data rates and sensing resolution. In such bands, Coordinated Beamforming (CoBF) will be a critical technique to mitigate performance degradation that can occur when highly directional links are occluded by mobile environmental obstructions. Moreover, due to decreased wavelength, sub-THz networks can increasingly operate in the near field, which yields non-planar wavefronts at receivers. In this paper, we present the first experimental study of receiver (RX) beamforming for sub-THz CoBF operating in the near field. Specifically, we introduce a suite of RX beamforming policies that span Channel State Information at the Receiver (CSIR) requirements as well as RX beamforming capabilities. At one extreme, we define a baseline RX beamforming policy that uses an electromagnetic wave model to compute CSIR, accounting for transmitter location, beam type, and near-field propagation characteristics; the RX then compensates for the computed phase profile over each RX array element to maximize coherent combining. At the other extreme, we consider strategies that, despite operating in the near field, employ far-field beam steering via a linear phase gradient at the receiver. Such policies are not only simple in CSIR requirements (not requiring phase information for each antenna element) but also simplify receiver configuration, requiring only a single parameter to characterize a linear phase gradient. We first experimentally study an unobstructed CoBF link and quantify the benefits of compensating for the nonlinear incident phase as compared to conventional far-field oriented methods. We then experimentally study obstructed links and measure the performance of the policies under partial blockage, as well as RX power improvement from real-time adaptation to blockage.

title: Strategic Client-Level Defense Placement in Mobile Federated Learning.
abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables mobile and edge devices to train jointly without centralizing private data, but compromised clients can poison the global model. When client-level protections cover only part of the population, a rational attacker can exploit predictable placement. We introduce SGDP-FL (Stackelberg Game-Based Defense Placement for Federated Learning), a budget-constrained Stackelberg game between a defender and an attacker. Before each round, the defender decides which clients to protect. The attacker observes this placement only through noisy reconnaissance, updates its belief about which clients are protected, and then chooses which clients to attack. We model the noisy observation as a Binary Symmetric Channel, and we model imperfect defenses by letting each protection block an attack only with a fixed probability. Monte Carlo estimation and a greedy knapsack oracle make the resulting bilevel problem tractable. We evaluate SGDP-FL on EMNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100 under IID and non-IID partitions. The evaluation covers single- and multi-client attacks, with attack targets either fixed or periodically reshuffled. In every tested setting, SGDP-FL achieves the highest mean accuracy among Random, Highest-Value, and UCB allocation. Under multi-client attacks with periodic reshuffling, it raises CIFAR-10 IID accuracy from 55.68% for the strongest baseline to 59.78%, and CIFAR-100 IID from 32.42% to 34.49%. It also transfers to label-flipping and backdoor attacks and complements robust aggregation.

title: Sharing of Irreversible Latent Features in lieu of RF IQ Data for Multiple Downstream Learning Tasks.
abstract: Wireless in-phase and quadrature (I/Q) data is useful for training various radio frequency (RF) machine learning (ML) models. However, sharing such I/Q data faces barriers from concerns of (i) potentially violating laws related to recording raw samples that can eventually be decoded by an unauthorized third party, and (ii) revealing information about a proprietary system or the environment involved in the data capture. This paper proposes a different solution to sharing I/Q data intended for use in ML models by leveraging latent embeddings obtained through a shared encoder. The key contributions include: (i) demonstrating how a single set of common features can be extracted from an I/Q dataset for training multiple downstream RF classification or regression tasks, (ii) designing a method of structured noise infusion that impairs the reverse recovery of the raw I/Q from the feature space without significant impact to the downstream tasks, and (iii) demonstrating the application of this method on informative real-world, publicly available datasets. Sharing well-constructed yet privacy-preserving features can accelerate foundational research on ML for wireless without relying on hard-to-get I/Q samples.

title: Continuous Semantic Caching for Low-Cost LLM Serving.
abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) become increasingly popular, caching responses so that they can be reused by users with semantically similar queries has become a vital strategy for reducing inference costs and latency. Existing caching frameworks have proposed to decide which query responses to cache by assuming a finite, known universe of discrete queries and learning their serving costs and arrival probabilities. As LLMs' pool of users and queries expands, however, such an assumption becomes increasingly untenable: real-world LLM queries reside in an infinite, continuous embedding space. In this paper, we establish the first rigorous theoretical framework for semantic LLM response caching in continuous query space under uncertainty. To bridge the gap between discrete optimization and continuous representation spaces, we introduce dynamic e-net discretization coupled with Kernel Ridge Regression. This design enables the system to formally quantify estimation uncertainty and generalize partial feedback on LLM query costs across continuous semantic query neighborhoods. We develop both offline learning and online adaptive algorithms optimized to reduce switching costs incurred by changing the cached responses. We prove that our online algorithm achieves a sublinear regret bound against an optimal oracle, which reduces to existing bounds for discrete query models. Extensive empirical evaluations demonstrate that our framework approximates the continuous optimal cache well while also reducing computational and switching overhead compared to existing methods.

title: Worse Routes, Fresher Information: Preemption Redefines Which Route is Best.
abstract: This paper studies joint sampling, route activation, and preemption control over N heterogeneous transmission routes under a long-run objective combining Age of Information (AoI) with sampling and transmission costs. We formulate the problem as an average-cost impulse-control model, derive a vector-form integral average-cost optimality equation over a hybrid state space, and establish structural reductions on the state. We consider a two-route case and compute optimized policies using discretized policy iteration. Surprisingly, the results show that preemption can reverse routing preferences: the optimized policy may exclusively use a route with both a larger mean delay and a larger delay variance while avoiding the seemingly superior route. Relative to baselines that do not allow preemption, the proposed policy reduces average AoI by up to 96%.

title: Controlled Radio Fault Injection and Telemetry Evaluation for Open 5G RANs.
abstract: Radio access network (RAN) telemetry reveals radio conditions, protocol behavior, and their consequences for applications. Evaluating its usefulness requires controlled impairments and observations of the same execution. We present C and Python channel brokers and a fault injection workflow for software 5G testbeds connecting an OCUDU base station and a software UE through ZeroMQ. The brokers apply scheduled, directional transformations to I/Q samples and restore the link, while the workflow jointly records applied faults, native and programmable (codelet) telemetry, and application delay. We demonstrate this capability through 45 comparative trials of brief uplink interruptions and stepped additive noise. These use cases distinguish recognizing a radio change from measuring its service consequence: native missing-feedback events retrospectively identify interruptions, whereas noise changes decoding-error measurements without producing those events. Median on-time round-trip times remain near 30 ms, but the prespecified comparisons show mean increases in on-time 95th-percentile delay of 354 and 604 ms for one and five interruptions, and 113 ms for noise. Adding receive-side radio link control (RLC) codelet summaries did not improve interruption classification on held-out trials. The framework provides a reusable way to evaluate measurement choices under known radio faults, before using them in monitoring or learning systems.

title: Measuring the Predictability of Beam-Level 5G Traffic: How Far Can Zero-Shot Foundation Models Go?
abstract: Beam-level traffic forecasting is critical for 5G resource allocation, yet the measurement properties of beam-level traffic remain poorly understood. We present a measurement-driven analysis across 2,961 time series from two public 5G datasets released by third parties. We first characterize how beam-level traffic differs from the aggregated cell-level traffic studied in prior work, identifying a sparsity-dependent predictability gradient: active beams exhibit the strongest periodicity and covariate correlations, enabling accurate forecasting, while covariate gains attenuate with sparsity until most methods converge on the sparsest beams. We then benchmark 16 model configurations, including four general-purpose Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) pre-trained without mobile-network data and one RAN-specific foundation model, across three experimental settings. A zero-shot TSFM given identical oracle covariates outperforms trained alternatives on 68-73% of beams (64% univariately), but this advantage is concentrated on active beams where periodic structure is strongest; on the sparsest beams, foundation and trained models converge to the same noise-dominated predictability floor. The dominant factor has to do with information inputs rather than the model architecture: oracle network telemetry covariates reduce error more than switching between any two general-purpose architectures, and covariate-augmented models are also more resilient to distribution shift. We interpret this benefit as an information-content upper bound: deployable pipelines that lag, extrapolate, or separately forecast the covariates recover none of the oracle gain at a one-week horizon, identifying covariate acquisition, rather than model choice, as the key open problem. Without future information, zero-shot Chronos-2 matches or beats trained univariate pipelines while requiring no training or retraining.

title: Latency Aware Zero Trust Authorization for Secure Mobile Edge Networks.
abstract: Mobile edge networks need techniques to manage security-risk and latency trade-offs across flexible identity, device, and context-aware trust, as well as network conditions. We develop a latency aware zero-trust approach that fuses fail-closed policy gates, a cost-sensitive gradient boosting classifier, and a latency predictor. Authorization is granted provided that the trust is satisfied for all identity, device, context, authentication, risk, and RBAC (Role-Based Access Control) elements. The predicted latency meets the service budget. Evaluation is conducted on resource-constrained mobile edge networks, using an access-request dataset with leakage-resistant features, stratified and entity-disjoint partitions, an asymmetric false-allow cost, and tail-latency measurements. The raw context classifier gave 99.10% accuracy, 0.978 macro F1, 0.956 MCC, and .294% false-allow rate, while the deterministic gate reproduced all policy labels. The results support secure authorization and confirm that edge computing can scale analytically. Our work also prioritizes measuring device-level latency before operational deployment at scale.

title: IoTell: Multimodal Sensor Fusion for Enhanced IoT Control.
abstract: Current control interfaces between users and heterogeneous IoT devices rely on device-specific applications or voice commands with a limited set of instructions. Such mechanisms do not scale to dense IoT networks, where users interact with tens of smart devices in everyday environments. Although RF-based ranging technologies enable accurate estimation of user location indoors, turning this spatial context into intuitive interaction remains an open challenge. We introduce IoTell, an interface that lets users control a device by pointing at it and speaking a short command. IoTell fuses location, orientation, and voice to identify the intended device, using an error-adaptive 3D candidate zone to resolve the target even when several devices are nearby. In the device-dependent mode, IoTell uses a wearable that provides location and orientation and opportunistically supplies labeled training data for the device-independent mode, which estimates them by fusing audio and RF features, offering a similar experience without a wearable. We implement IoTell with a UWB-based localization system and evaluate it in a multi-device indoor environment, achieving 95.2% command-execution accuracy in the device-dependent setting and, in the device-independent setting, 88.3% localization accuracy with orientation predicted within 20° at 78.4% accuracy. Multimodal fusion of spatial and linguistic context can substantially improve interaction with IoT systems under realistic conditions.

title: Private 5G Security Across Public and Non-Public Networks: A Cross-Deployment Analysis.
abstract: Private 5G networks are increasingly deployed in industrial, healthcare, and defence settings, yet existing 5G security studies offer little systematic insight into how the same security problem changes across deployment models. We compile a corpus of 25 security cases from 3GPP requirements and prior 5G threat and risk analyses, spanning eSIMs and UEs, the RAN, and the 5G Core, and examine six illustrative cases in detail. Using a Public Land Mobile Network (PLMN) as the reference, we compare Standalone Non-Public Networks (SNPNs) and Public Network Integrated NPNs (PNI-NPNs) in terms of applicability, attack feasibility, and network-level technical consequence, and explain the differences through four dimensions: attack reachability, administrative control and trust, security-control state, and resilience topology. We find that feasibility and consequence can change independently: restricted access can make access-dependent attacks harder, while limited redundancy can increase the impact of compromise or failure. For PNI-NPNs, the effect is function-specific and depends on function placement, sharing, and operational responsibility. Finally, we relate these network-level effects to industrial, healthcare, and tactical use cases.

title: Windex: Index-Driven Contextual Scheduler for Scalable Service Guarantees in NextG Cellular Networks.
abstract: Next-generation cellular networks must support heterogeneous service objectives, ranging from throughput-oriented eMBB to latency- and regularity-constrained URLLC and XR traffic. Enforcing these objectives at the RAN scheduler is difficult because wireless channels, queues, and application arrivals evolve at the millisecond timescale while spectrum resources are shared across users. We formulate service-aware RAN scheduling as a constrained Markov decision process with per-user throughput and service-regularity constraints. A Lagrangian relaxation gives an exact decomposition of the relaxed problem into per-user control problems with a common resource price. We prove fixed-dual indexability for an illustrative time-since-last-service (TSLS) debt arm with a throughput objective and TSLS constraint, note the analogous scalar throughput-debt result, and assume fixed-dual indexability for the full vector state used in deployment. We design Windex, an index-driven scheduler that learns dual-dependent per-user break-even resource prices using compact neural approximators over queue, channel, TSLS, and violation-deficit state. We further design CWindex, a contextual extension that infers service class from queue-history time series when explicit labels are unavailable. We implement Windex as an application compatible with a realtime 5G radio intelligent controller. Inference takes 10-20 μs per user on a general-purpose CPU, well within a 1 ms control budget. Trace-driven emulation using over-the-air channel measurements and larger simulations show that Windex and CWindex substantially reduce per-user service violations while maintaining throughput efficiency.

title: Trust-Driven Multi-Criteria Aerial Networking for Mission-Critical IoT with Localization Uncertainty.
abstract: Aerial edge computing brings Internet of things (IoT) connectivity and computation to mission-critical and underserved environments, where reliability depends on trustworthy aerial elements. Spatial perturbations from dynamic IoT devices distort trust judgments and raise the risk of unreliable UAV selection and task failure. Trust estimation therefore links directly to network resilience in mission-critical operations. We propose a confidence-calibrated hybrid trust framework that uses uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) and high-altitude platforms (HAPs) to support reliable task offloading and collaborative inference. The trust model hybridizes dependent and independent performance indicators through a reliability factor that calibrates confidence in trust estimation. We formulate a multi-criteria optimization problem that maximizes trust, enhances IoT connectivity, and minimizes total latency while accounting for spatial perturbations of IoT devices and system constraints. A penalty-guided optimization (PGO) algorithm solves this problem by combining a penalty term with sequential quadratic programming to recover near-binary solutions. The optimization also guides UAVs to adjust their positions based on IoT device distribution, which balances coverage and improves computational efficiency. We compare PGO against branch-and-bound, greedy, and baseline relaxation algorithms. Simulation results show that PGO consistently yields high-quality solutions at tractable computational cost. These findings support trust-driven, resilient, and low-latency aerial computing for mission-critical 6G IoT networks.

title: mmPoison: Targeted Clean-label Poisoning Attacks on mmWave-based Human Activity Recognition.
abstract: Nowadays, mmWave-based human activity recognition (HAR) systems are widely used in smart homes, healthcare monitoring, and telemedicine. To achieve high accuracy, HAR systems require large-scale data collection from distributed sources for model training, such as edge devices or public repositories, which opens up opportunities for attackers to inject poisoned data into the training process, inducing false predictions and damaging the reliability of mmWave-based HAR systems. This paper presents targeted clean-label poisoning attack strategies, mmPoison, which injects imperceptible poisoned data into the training datasets for causing misclassifications on target instances in mmWave-based HAR systems without controlling the labeling process. In mmPoison, different attack methodologies are proposed for different attacker capabilities. For white-box setting, discriminative region masking is used to limit perturbations in discriminative regions. Then, mmPoison updates perturbations based on parameter trajectory alignment, and optimizes the poisoned instances to remain close to the clean instances. This process is iteratively applied to generate poisoned datasets. For black-box setting, mmPoison trains surrogate models with pseudo-label supervision and then uses them in a generator-discriminator framework to generate poisoned instances by jointly optimizing attack effectiveness and imperceptibility. Experiments conducted on public and self-collected datasets validate the effectiveness and imperceptibility of mmPoison in causing misclassifications within mmWave-based HAR systems.

title: Less Federation, More Personalization: One-Shot Multi-View Clustering for Federated Fall Detection.
abstract: Federated learning is a natural fit for sensor-based fall detection, where data are privacy-sensitive and highly non-IID across subjects. A two-stage framework is proposed in which each client first learns label-free representations using FMMVCC, a multi-view clustering encoder that combines reconstruction, cross-view consistency, contrastive learning, and prototype-based objectives. The resulting encoders are then aggregated via a single round of FedAvg into a shared frozen feature extractor, decoupling representation learning from downstream classification. Experiments are conducted on the FallTL dataset, a wearable sensing benchmark evaluated under both binary (Fall/ADL) and 16-class (activity × Fall/ADL) granularities. Results show that FMMVCC achieves strong representation quality, outperforming four self-supervised baselines in binary classification (84.15% ACC) and providing competitive performance in the fine-grained setting. On top of these representations, the personalized closed-form classifier consistently outperforms FedAvg, FedProx, and shared analytic baselines by 8-13pp, and matches or exceeds FedProto in the 16-class setting while requiring no communication during inference. Finally, cross-client alignment metrics are shown to be weak predictors of downstream performance, while class-separability measures correlate more reliably with accuracy.

title: Democratizing LoRa Weak Signal Demodulation.
abstract: This paper democratizes LoRa weak signal demodulation from both the methodological and experimental perspectives. Methodologically, by drawing inspiration from LoRa's CSS modulation principle, this paper proposes DeLoRa, the first lightweight neural-enhanced method for LoRa weak signal demodulation which can be executed on LoRa nodes possessing far more limited hardware resources than LoRa gateways. Experimentally, this paper proposes MCU-SDR, the first hardware testbed that matches the stringent resource constraints of LoRa nodes, enabling LoRa researchers to carry out in-situ evaluation of demodulation methods for LoRa nodes. Our extensive evaluation in indoor and outdoor environments shows that DeLoRa operates effectively (i.e., ensures <10% symbol error rate) at SNR level as low as -18.8 dB, achieving a 3.3 dB SNR gain over SOTA demodulation methods that can run on LoRa nodes.

title: Balancing Synchronization and Sum Delay in Cloud Virtual Reality Applications.
abstract: This paper addresses the joint optimization of synchronization delay and total motion-to-photon latency in multiuser interactive cloud-based virtual reality systems. We propose a rendering strategy that switches each user between local and cloud rendering to balance synchronization and sum delay. While prior studies have optimized either inter-user synchronization delay or sum delay independently, we define and analyze the Balanced Delay Optimization (BDO) problem under a constraint on the number of cloud-rendered users. We prove that BDO is NP-hard in general. Under a cloud-faster-than-local condition, which induces a submodular regime, we identify a polynomial-time solvable unconstrained case and, for the NP-hard constrained case, develop a minimum s-t cut-based approximation algorithm with a provable suboptimality bound, and show that it runs within a 90 Hz VR frame budget over the tested range. Numerical simulations and Unity-based prototype experiments validate the proposed framework. In particular, the proposed algorithm closely tracks the exact optimum in the submodular regime and remains competitive in a non-submodular violation-case simulation.

title: CEDAR: Structure-Aware Contrastive Learning for One-Class Network Intrusion Detection.
abstract: Intrusion detection remains a critical challenge in modern networks. Existing approaches primarily attempt to detect attacks by identifying anomalies in network flow features, which is significantly challenged by the high cost of labeling, the limited availability of attack data, and the heterogeneous and continually evolving nature of attack techniques. In this paper, we propose CEDAR, a one-class feature-based detector that requires only benign traffic data for training, by integrating weakly structured contrastive representation learning with von Mises-Fisher mixture modeling in the latent space. CEDAR leverages communication context derived from source-destination interactions as a form of weak supervision to learn structure-aware embeddings, eliminating the need for synthetic flow augmentations. Furthermore, it jointly learns the encoder and the von Mises-Fisher mixture density parameters under a unified objective with proven convergence guarantees. Comprehensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves favorable performance compared with a diverse set of intrusion detection baselines.

title: AOTP: Towards Application-Agnostic Network Transport for Data Freshness.
abstract: Minimizing Age of Information (AoI) is critical for time-sensitive applications, yet a gap remains between AoI optimization theory and practical implementation. Existing solutions face two main barriers: application-layer approaches often rely on application-specific control logic, limiting reuse across applications, while link-layer approaches require network software or firmware changes that hinder broad deployment. We introduce the Age-Oriented Transport Protocol (AOTP), a transport-layer protocol for application-agnostic AoI optimization. AOTP separates freshness control from application logic by managing network estimation, update selection, and transmission timing. Its Sampling Mode (AOTP-S) combines Robbins-Monro threshold learning with timeout recovery and change detection to adapt sampling to network dynamics. Its Decoupled Mode (AOTP-D) combines single-packet replacement with delay-gradient pacing for independently generated updates. Extensive ns-3 simulations cover mobile WiFi links, dense multi-flow networks, and hybrid wired-wireless paths. AOTP-S reduces average AoI by up to 74.3% relative to ACP+ on a mobile link. With 16 contending flows, AOTP-D reduces the geometric mean of normalized AoI by approximately 98.4%. AOTP also preserves fairness among update flows and maintains service for competing TCP traffic.

title: Poster: Time-Critical Information Relaying via Multi-UAVs in Disconnected Environments.
abstract: Rapid information transmission in disconnected environments is critical for applications such as post-disaster assessment. Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) can efficiently construct a multi-hop communication network to relay information from the damaged area to the command center. In this work, a heuristic approach reduces the mission completion time by both UAV-based network construction and trajectory planning. Simulation results show that the approach can achieve an average 30.26% reduction in completion time.

title: FrozenSFL: Model-Frozen Split Federated Learning for Resource-Efficient LLM Fine-Tuning over Heterogeneous Edge Devices.
abstract: Collaborative fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs) at the network edge enables privacy-preserving and personalized generative intelligence, but is constrained by the limited memory and compute resources of edge devices. Traditional approaches, such as split federated learning (SFL), partition models between devices and a server, requiring iterative exchanges of activations/gradients while the server manages multiple submodels. This leads to substantial communication overhead, high activation storage costs, and severe server-side memory pressure when scaling to massive heterogeneous devices. In this paper, we propose FrozenSFL, a resource-efficient SFL framework for collaborative fine-tuning of LLMs across heterogeneous edge devices. At its core, FrozenSFL strictly freezes device-side submodels to eliminate both deviceside backpropagation and server-to-device gradient transmission, thereby removing on-device activation storage requirements and downlink communication overhead. Building upon this design, we improve the framework in two aspects. First, we design a layerwise LoRA aggregation strategy to handle structural heterogeneity introduced by device-specific model partitioning and enable efficient server-side updates. Second, we introduce a server-side feature caching mechanism that reuses invariant features, allowing subsequent training epochs to proceed offline and reducing redundant computation and communication. We implement the FrozenSFL system as an asynchronous multi-threaded pipeline, which serves as our real-world testbed for evaluation. On the device side, forward computation and data transmission are decoupled via a producer-consumer mechanism. On the server side, a first-in-first-out scheduling strategy serializes fine-tuning tasks across devices. A hybrid memory-disk streaming mechanism further buffers incoming data and ensures stable training under network variability. Extensive evaluations with representative models, including BERT-Base (0.11B), ViT-Large (0.3B), and LLaMA-2-7B (7B), validate the effectiveness of FrozenSFL. In particular, for LLaMA-2-7B, FrozenSFL can reduce device/server VRAM footprint by up to 14%/82.7% with only 1% accuracy loss, while achieving up to 6.7× fine-tuning speedup.

title: CREWS: Collaborative Robust Edge WiFi Sensing with Asynchronous and Incomplete Observations.
abstract: Existing collaborative WiFi sensing systems rely on perfect node synchronization and complete data availability. However, real-world edge deployments suffer from heterogeneous computing and network dropouts, leading to asynchronous and incomplete features. We propose CREWS, a robust collaborative sensing framework that inherently resists these network volatility. First, CREWS employs a topology-agnostic aggregator that is invariant to arrival order and supports variable receiver subsets. Second, rather than discarding delayed observations, it utilizes a staleness-aware adaptive replay mechanism. By treating stale features from lagging nodes as system-induced hard samples, CREWS transforms synchronization delays into beneficial training regularization. We derive a joint optimization bound that characterizes the resulting stationarity neighborhood and the trade-off between replay bias and variance. Extensive evaluations and an 8-node heterogeneous hardware testbed demonstrate its superior resilience. Under severe conditions i.e., 50% transient dropout rate, CREWS restricts accuracy degradation to merely 2.3 percentage points, substantially outperforming state-of-the-art WiFi Sensing baselines.

title: Performance Evaluation of Maritime Private 5G Networks: Impact of UPF Placement, Satellite Class, and Cloud Resource Sizing.
abstract: Providing private 5G networks onboard ships is challenging due to the reliance on non-terrestrial backhaul connectivity and the need to balance service performance with limited onboard computing resources. This paper investigates deployment architectures for maritime private 5G networks, where the radio access network is located onboard the ship while core network functions are deployed either locally or within shore-side cloud infrastructure. We compare candidate architectures by analyzing the placement of the User Plane Function (UPF) between the ship and remote datacenters, and evaluate the impact of satellite link class and cloud resource sizing on throughput and latency. The study considers ship-to-shore connectivity over satellite links, emulating GEO, MEO, and LEO conditions, along with shore-side core deployments in Luanda (Angola) and Lagos (Nigeria). Experimental results based on iPerf and ping measurements show that an onboard UPF configuration achieves the lowest latency and best overall performance, whereas remote UPF deployments are significantly affected by satellite delay. Increasing virtual machine resources in shore-side deployments improves throughput, particularly under MEO and LEO scenarios, but does not significantly reduce latency when the satellite path remains the dominant source of delay. Furthermore, placing the shore-side gateway closer to the satellite gateway yields better performance compared to more distant datacenter deployments. These findings highlight key deployment trade-offs in maritime private 5G systems and support the design of hybrid onboard/shore architectures for latency-sensitive services.

title: WiimtPlaim: Conversational Digital Twin-based Layout Planning for Intent-Preserving RF Optimization.
abstract: Factory layouts shape millimeter-wave propagation, yet RF-effective rearrangements can obstruct routes, violate process rules, or degrade other clients. We present WintPlan, a human-in-the-loop system that turns reactive service deficits and proactive deployment requests into intent-preserving physical reconfigurations. An RF digital twin identifies movable contributors, while operators express and refine operational intent through natural language and marked regions. An intent adapter grounds these inputs into persistent factory knowledge, and a deterministic compiler converts active rules into executable global and relative placement affinities that constrain RF-aware layout search, separating language interpretation from placement generation and RF evaluation while preserving learned site-specific intent across later interventions. In a calibrated 288 m2 cryogenic facility, WintPlan recovers ≈ 57 Mbps of target throughput on average while preserving all applicable hard rules and retaining over 90% of RF-Only's gain. The trained adapter improves exact grounded-rule recovery from 17.9-28.1% to 33.3-62.3% across In-Distribution and Out-Of-Distribution splits. Across 20 six-intervention sequences, 75% complete within two operator corrections and all within four; semantic pruning reduces full ray-tracing evaluations from 256 to 104 at a 256-candidate budget with 100% search success.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Morpheus: Interactive RF Digital Twins for In-Situ Layout Orchestration in Dynamic mmWave Environments.
abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) networks provide high wireless capacity, but remain fragile in indoor environments, where small layout changes disrupt dominant propagation paths causing performance degradation. Automated RF planners optimize throughput but ignore operational constraints (or intents) that are difficult to enumerate or encode a priori, often producing infeasible layout configurations. Meanwhile human operators enforce feasibility but lack RF awareness. We present Morpheus, an interactive, human-in-the-loop framework for proactive, in-situ layout orchestration in mmWave environments. Morpheus bridges this gap through a human-in-the-loop design, leveraging an RF-aware digital twin to help recommend plausible future layout adjustments. This improves throughput while preserving intent through learned layout-priors and user feedback. We evaluate Morpheus on two real-world industrial deployments, where it improves throughput by 25-40% over human-driven layouts while remaining close to intent-aligned configurations, reducing the overhead of intent violations by 2-3×, and achieves comparable throughput to automated planners with significantly fewer intent violations.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Efficient Secure Federated Learning via Information-Theoretically Secure Key Distribution: A Medical Imaging Case Study.
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative training of models across institutions without centralizing sensitive data, making it well-suited for privacy-concerned applications, such as medical imaging. To protect FL model updates during secure aggregation, additive masking is commonly employed. However, its underlying classical key establishment is only computationally secure. On the other hand, physics-based Information-Theoretically Secure (ITS) key exchange introduces practical constraints: finite key generation rates and time-limited storage severely limit throughput and sustained training of uncompressed models. In this work, we address this bottleneck by developing an FL framework that integrates frozen backbones, knowledge distillation, and quantization. These techniques reduce communication payload and, consequently, key material consumption. Moving beyond simulation, we benchmark this framework on a real physics-based key distribution testbed involving a chest X-ray classification application. Our results show that key usage can be reduced by ~35× while maintaining predictive accuracy. This prevents buffer depletion and key expiration, enabling sustainable FL training under physical key generation constraints.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Reliable V2X-Enabled Autonomous Driving with Explainable Federated Neuro-Symbolic Intelligence.
abstract: Connected and autonomous vehicles rely on vehicle-to-everything (V2X) cooperation when local sensing is incomplete or delayed, as often occurs in dense traffic, occluded intersections, and roads with constrained communication. Yet many data-driven driving models remain difficult to interpret, and centralized learning requires large raw sensory data transfers that raise communication and privacy concerns. This paper proposes an explainable federated neuro-symbolic intelligence framework for reliable V2X-enabled autonomous driving. The framework combines neural perception, symbolic rule-based reasoning, fuzzy uncertainty modeling, and reliability-aware federated learning. Each vehicle trains a local decision agent from local driving and communication-context observations, while an edge or roadside unit aggregates model updates without collecting raw sensory data. The local agent also produces an interpretable rationale, including activated rules, uncertainty indicators, and risk factors associated with the selected decision. Simulation-based V2X results show that the proposed method improves decision quality, reduces missed safety-critical states, and converges faster than standard Federated Averaging (FedAvg) under vehicle-side data that are not independent and identically distributed (non-IID).
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Model-based Zero-shot Conflict Detection Framework via Gradients in O-RAN.
abstract: Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) enables network control through multi-vendor xApps operating both within and across layers, subnets, and domains, whose concurrent execution can trigger conflicts that are latent during the development phase. Existing conflict management approaches rely heavily on joint-execution data, which is often unavailable in practice. To address this limitation, we formalize a novel problem termed conflict reasoning, which involves identifying conflict-inducing conditions given only marginal datasets from each individual xApp. We propose ZODIAC, a three-stage framework for zero-shot conflict condition inference that comprises uncertainty-aware surrogate model training, trajectory-level diffusion training, and compositional guided denoising for efficient, physics-constrained, and reliable condition search. We derive a theoretical lower confidence bound showing that the compositional reasoning in ZODIAC serves as a principled surrogate for true conflict severity, with the epistemic penalty directly controlling the approximation gap. We evaluate ZODIAC on both the lightweight Mobile-Env platform across all three O-RAN Alliance conflict types (direct, indirect, and implicit) and a realistic NS-O-RAN-Flexric simulator. ZODIAC consistently outperforms baseline condition search methods, achieving over 20% higher True Positive Rate at Top-20, substantially stronger Spearman rank correlation, greater scenario diversity, and competitive computational efficiency. Ablation studies confirm the necessity of each guidance component, with epistemic uncertainty penalties proving essential for filtering spurious conflicts. To the best of our knowledge, ZODIAC is the first framework in O-RAN that enables conflict reasoning from marginal offline data without requiring any joint-execution traces.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: BatStation: Toward In-Situ Radar Sensing on 5G Base Stations with Zero-Shot Template Generation.
abstract: The coexistence between incumbent radar signals and commercial 5G signals demands a ubiquitous radar sensing for efficient and adaptive spectrum sharing. In this context, leveraging the densely deployed 5G base stations (BS) for radar sensing is particularly promising, offering both wide coverage and immediate feedback to 5G scheduling. However, the coexisting radar signals are superimposed on concurrent 5G uplink transmissions received by the BS, and practical deployment also demands a lightweight, portable radar sensing model. This paper presents BatStation, a lightweight, in-situ radar sensing framework seamlessly integrated into 5G BSs, which leverages uplink resource grids to extract radar signals through three key components: (i) radar signal separation to cancel concurrent 5G transmissions and reveal the radar signals, (ii) resource grid reshaping to align time-frequency resolution with radar pulse characteristics, and (iii) a zero-shot template correlation-based model that is trained purely on synthetic data that supports detection, classification, and localization of radar pulses, and can be directly applied to experiments. We implement BatStation on a software-defined radio (SDR) testbed and evaluate with real 5G traffic in the CBRS band. Results show robust performance across diverse radar types, achieving per-pulse detection probabilities of 97.02-79.23%, classification accuracy of 97.00%, and localization errors of 2.68-6.20 MHz (frequency) and 24.6-32.4 μs (time). Notably, BatStation requires runtime latency of only 0.11/0.94 ms on GPU/CPU, meeting the real-time requirement of 5G networks.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Just Talk Once: Communication-Efficient Split Federated LLM Fine-Tuning on Edge Devices.
abstract: Large language model (LLM) fine-tuning is increasingly shifting toward data generated on edge devices, where memory, computation, bandwidth, and connectivity constraints make conventional federated learning difficult to sustain. Split federated fine-tuning (SFT) improves client-side efficiency by offloading most model parameters and computation to the server but requires step-by-step bidirectional communication loop across the split interface and forces continuous client involvement throughout training. In this paper, we present L-shaped SFT, a split fine-tuning framework that removes this bidirectional bottleneck. Our key insight is that weight tying in modern LLMs enables server-side hidden activations to be directly supervised using target embeddings, allowing the training loss to be computed on the server without returning server outputs to the client. To further eliminate the need for continuous client participation, based on L-shaped SFT, we introduce one-shot SFT, in which clients upload activations once and then go offline while the server continues optimization over cached representations. We implement our design in a real system testbed with heterogeneous edge clients, including commercial smartphones and NVIDIA developer boards. Experiments demonstrate that our schemes significantly reduce communication costs and client online time compared with existing SFT baselines.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Communication-Aware Model Distributed Inference via Latent Representation Compression.
abstract: We study optimization of distributed model inference over resource-constrained edge resources. We propose a framework that optimizes the trade-off between model accuracy and communication costs by controlling latent representation compression to meet strict Quality of Service (QoS) throughput targets. For settings with known channel state information (CSI), we derive a closed-form optimal solution for single tasks and reduce the multi-task problem to a convex optimization program characterized by a per-link water-filling strategy. We extend these to handle unpredictable environments via a stochastic dual descent algorithm that relies only on causal channel estimates. We provide Lyapunov-based proofs demonstrating that our approach strictly satisfies long-term delay constraints while achieving a bounded optimality gap. Our results offer a robust, scalable blueprint for maximizing the performance of pipelined AI tasks in dynamic, resource-constrained distributed systems. We verify the effectiveness of our proposed framework through simulations and experiments with real edge devices.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: A Tale of Two Learning Algorithms: Multiple Stream Random Walk and Asynchronous Gossip.
abstract: Although gossip and random walk-based learning algorithms are widely known for decentralized learning, there has been limited theoretical and experimental analysis to understand their relative performance for different graph topologies and data heterogeneity. We first design and analyze an asynchronous random walk-based learning algorithm with multiple streams (walks), which we name “Multi-Walk”. We provide a convergence analysis for Multi-Walk with respect to the number of iterations (computation), wall-clock time, and communication cost. We also present a convergence analysis for “Asynchronous Gossip”, addressing the notable gap in the existing literature by explicitly accounting for its computational and communication overhead. Our results show that Multi-Walk has better convergence in terms of iterations as compared to Asynchronous Gossip in graphs with large diameters (e.g., cycles), while its relative performance, as compared to Asynchronous Gossip, depends on the number of walks and the data heterogeneity in graphs with small diameters (e.g., complete graphs). In wall-clock time analysis, we observe a linear speed-up with the number of walks and nodes in Multi-Walk and Asynchronous Gossip, respectively. Finally, we show that Multi-Walk outperforms Asynchronous Gossip in communication overhead, except in small-diameter topologies with extreme data heterogeneity. These results highlight the effectiveness of each algorithm across varying graph topologies and levels of data heterogeneity. Our code is available for reproducibility.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Time to Protection in Federated Intrusion Detection on Jetson Orin Nano Clusters.
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) allows IoT devices to improve a shared intrusion detector without exchanging raw data. A device, however, can only learn from attacks that reach it, and because federated detection is evaluated as a whole for the fleet of IoT devices or averaged over attack classes, it is not reported how long a device that has never observed an attack class remains exposed to it without protection. The aim of this paper is to measure that exposure window, round by round, and to determine how it depends on the share of the fleet that already holds the class. We deployed a federated system with nine clients on two Jetson Orin Nano clusters connected over a WAN. As the main dataset, we used N-BaIoT, which covers two devices that were never infected by the mirai attack. It was tested with one to seven attacked clients and validated on CWRU and PAMAP2 datasets. The results showed that new class arrival depends on the share of the fleet that already knows about it, reaching 0.827 on mirai after one round when trained from the start with mirai data on seven out of nine clients, and reaching protection thresholds after 4, 17, and 39 rounds for seven, three, and two of nine clients attacked, when the model was initially trained without knowledge of mirai. Our findings show that federation delivers recognition of an attack class quickly when much of the fleet already holds it, and slowly or not within our horizon when only a few devices have been hit, which is the case a defender is most concerned with.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Per-Request Paid Edge Inference for Unaffiliated Devices with Jetson Orin Nano.
abstract: Edge sites equipped with powerful on-device accelerators can serve low-latency inference services to IoT devices around them, and in a lot of cases, some of their capacity might be unused. In most cases, access to that unused computing power is impossible, as it would usually require a pre-created account, a dedicated API key, or a shared operator, which a lot of passing-by devices like delivery robots or inspection drones might not have. The aim of this paper is to evaluate whether an edge inference node can serve passing-by IoT devices that have no prior relationship with it, charging them for each request, without an explicit sign-up or enrollment, and to measure what that mechanism costs the edge site. For the purposes of this paper, we designed and built such a node, which can serve unknown devices, using unsettled request exposure as a resource, deployed on a three-board Jetson Orin Nano Super cluster, performing object detection on images using a YOLOv26 detector. It was tested with Raspberry Pi 5 serving as a client device, running up to 12 concurrent clients, with detailed measurements of latency and resource utilization, including an experiment with a 30-minute settlement outage. The experiments confirmed timely request processing and successful payment settlement, with reliable tracking of outstanding payments. Our findings show that per-request payment could be a practical way of opening idle edge accelerator computing capacity to stranger IoT devices.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Resilient Priority-Aware Inference for Mission-Critical UAV Networks Under Bursty Edge Load.
abstract: Mission-critical mobile networks, including UAV-based disaster-response systems, must keep delivering usable and trustworthy inference under the exact conditions that make inference harder: constrained edge compute, degraded backhaul, and requests arriving in bursts rather than at a steady rate. A system that allocates compute uniformly has no way to fail gracefully once a burst exceeds its budget, dropping high-urgency requests along with low-urgency ones. In this paper, we present a priority-aware admission-control architecture built around two trust mechanisms: a lightweight router that assigns each request a priority level grounded in verifiable evidence rather than a model confidence, and a deterministic safety gate that rejects unsafe outputs regardless of which model checkpoint produced them. Low- and medium-priority requests are served by a baseline checkpoint, and a confidence-gated escalation path that reserves a more capable checkpoint for requests that need it. Both mechanisms are designed as auditable security controls rather than opaque model judgments: the router functions as a content-based access-control decision, and the safety gate as a policy-enforcement point that cannot be bypassed by manipulating the model confidence. We evaluate this policy end-to-end. The priority queue degrades gracefully, exactly as designed, under a simulated burst load. The router and confidence gate that feed it, however, correctly protect only 46.58% of genuinely high-priority requests, and a policy-optimization stage did not measurably improve the underlying checkpoint. Ultimately, a safety mechanism is only as trustworthy as the evidence behind it.

title: Demo: Multimodal Stress Monitoring with Split Federated Fine-Tuning on Mobile Devices.
abstract: We present an end-to-end mobile system for proactive stress monitoring from wearable signals. The framework is supported by an extensible split federated learning system that enables on-device LoRA fine-tuning of large language models. By analyzing physiological data, the application distinguishes emotional states, summarizes recent trends, and provides brief, actionable suggestions. Upon detecting a negative emotional state, the paired smartwatch or smartphone proactively delivers notifications to users to encourage mindfulness. The on-site demonstration will showcase real-time sensing-inference on smartwatch-phone pairs, alongside a recorded split federated learning process that continuously learns from user private data. Our code has been open-sourced at: https://github.com/HKU-WILL-Lab/Multimodal-Stress-Monitoring-with-Split-Federated-Fine-Tuning-on-Mobile-Devices.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Topology-Aware Sparse Attention for Intrusion Detection in Communication Networks.
abstract: Intrusion detection in communication networks faces challenges due to complex feature interactions and class imbalance. This paper proposes a topology-aware sparse attention model that captures structured dependencies among features using a correlation-based topology mask. By constraining attention to topologically relevant feature pairs, the proposed approach reduces computational complexity while improving interpretability and robustness. The model is evaluated on the UNSW-NB15 dataset, focusing on Backdoor and Shellcode attacks, and incorporates class-weight balancing to address data imbalance. Experimental results demonstrate superior performance, achieving 95.49% accuracy and an AUC of 0.983, outperforming state-of-the-art models including Transformer variants and recurrent networks. Additionally, the model achieves high throughput with low latency, making it suitable for real-time deployment in modern communication systems.

title: Poster: Improving Delay-Based Congestion Control on WiFi Uplinks with Local TX-Completion Feedback.
abstract: Delay-based congestion control algorithms (CCAs), such as Copa and Vegas, often underutilize WiFi uplinks because end-to-end RTT conflates true queue buildup with wireless effects, including channel contention, rate adaptation, and TCP ACK-path delay. We present TIDE (Transmission-completion Informed Delay Estimation), a cross-layer scheme that exploits WiFi NIC transmission (TX)-completion events to derive a host-side delay signal for the local transmit path. TIDE refines the delay signal exposed to legacy delay-based CCAs by complementing receiver feedback with local WiFi delay information, and integrates into the TCP stack without modifying the core control logic of existing CCAs. Experiments on a commodity WiFi testbed show that TIDE substantially improves throughput with only moderate delay increase under contention and weak-signal conditions. In particular, under contention, TIDE improves the throughput of Copa and Vegas by 55.0% and 236.6%, respectively.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Quantum-Inspired Semantic Communication Capacity Analysis based on von Neumann Entropy.
abstract: Semantic communication aims to transmit the task-relevant uncertainty that remains after common knowledge has been taken into account. However, the semantic communication capacity and rate distortion analysis have not been well investigated theoretically. Inspired by quantum entanglement across a black-hole horizon, this paper develops a quantum-inspired framework, where we present a von Neumann entropy bridge between new information and existing common knowledge. Conditioned on the existing common knowledge and the new information, we show that the corresponding von Neumann entropy is continuous and nondecreasing. To give this von Neumann entropy a practical interpretation, we define an auxiliary classical spectral-mode source, whose conditional probabilities are the eigenvalues of the reduced state. Then the resulting semantic capacity and tradeoff are discussed between the fully new information (the Shannon capacity case) and fully common knowledge (no new information) limits. Furthermore, we derive a conditional rate-distortion function, a source-channel feasibility condition, and a task-specific semantic-sample throughput over a cost-constrained discrete memoryless channel. A binary example illustrates the effects of common knowledge, semantic distinguishability, distortion tolerance, and the physical channel capacity.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Asymptotically Optimal Joint Generation-Planning and Transmission-Scheduling for Periodic Deadline-Constrained Wireless Communication.
abstract: We study the joint design of packet generation-planning and transmission-scheduling for periodic, deadline-constrained wireless communication. While transmission scheduling has been extensively studied in the literature, the generation planning problem has been largely neglected. However, a poor packet generation plan (e.g., when all sources generate new packets at the same time) causes high latency that cannot be overcome by transmission scheduling alone. We propose a new joint offline-online optimization framework for this problem, in which generation timing is optimized offline to spread arrivals evenly across time, while online transmission decisions are made via a Whittle index scheduling policy. Interestingly, we find that the Whittle index policy by itself (obtained through a standard relaxed problem) may not be asymptotically optimal given an arbitrary generation plan. Instead, it becomes asymptotically optimal only after we jointly design the generation plan (based on the solution to the same relaxed problem). We prove that our joint solution is asymptotically optimal under assumptions/conditions of uniform global attractivity, uniform local stability, and peak-smoothing. Our proof requires new techniques that capture the periodic and time-inhomogeneous nature of the system and that overcome the difficulty due to the generation plans changing with the system scale. We verify our stated assumptions and optimality results through simulations, and show that our joint solution achieves substantially lower latency plus deadline-violation costs than other baselines.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Demo: Software-Based Restricted Access Window for Industrial IoT Networks.
abstract: Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) applications require highly reliable data transmission. This is challenging in heterogeneous scenarios, where mission-critical data coexist with heavy traffic, such as video streams, on a single network. Wi-Fi HaLow addresses this issue by offering relatively high throughput and providing the Restricted Access Window (RAW) for scheduled access. However, most existing Wi-Fi HaLow devices do not support RAW due to hardware complexity. This study demonstrates the use of Software-Based RAW (SB-RAW) in a heterogeneous network. SB-RAW allows low-cost Wi-Fi HaLow devices to schedule channel access without hardware modifications. The demonstration shows that SB-RAW reduces jitter for mission-critical data and meets latency requirements without degrading concurrent video transmission performance in an IIoT network prototype.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Bridge: Optimizing Collective Communication Schedules in Reconfigurable Networks with Reusable Subrings.
abstract: Optical circuit-switched networks have emerged as an appealing alternative to electrical fabrics as they can reconfigure the network topology at runtime, reducing communication cost and improving bandwidth utilization. Yet exploiting optical reconfigurable networks for collective communication comes with a fundamental trade-off: each reconfiguration incurs non-negligible delay and the benefit of a new topology depends on future traffic. The central question is therefore when reconfiguration is worth its cost. While prior work has demonstrated the benefits of reconfiguration, the opportunity to reuse optical links to optimize multiple steps remains largely unexplored. In this paper, we present B ridge , a reconfiguration strategy for frequently used collective communication primitives, namely All-to-All, AllReduce, Reduce-Scatter, and AllGather. B ridge exploits the structure of Bruck's communication pattern to support efficient sparse reconfiguration. The key idea is to reduce propagation and transmission delay by directly connecting immediate communication partners and preserve efficient reachability to future peers through connected subrings . As a result, optical links can be reused across multiple subsequent steps, allowing the benefit of reconfiguration to amortize beyond a single step. Our evaluation shows that B ridge reduces All-to-All completion time by typically 3× to 10× over static baselines and is effective even with millisecond-scale reconfiguration delays; for AllReduce up to 1.5× against existing reconfiguration strategies, and by 1.5× to 6.6× against the R ing algorithm on low to moderate-sized workloads.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Demo: Vision-Language Model-Guided Online Calibration of an Electromagnetic Digital Twin.
abstract: An electromagnetic (EM) digital twin gives mobile robots wireless situational awareness but depends on material conductivities that change with the environment. Online calibration faces initialization sensitivity and measurement travel costs. We demonstrate a vision-language model (VLM)-guided framework using a Unitree G1 robot and NVIDIA Sionna, with two VLM calls: material classification maps visible materials through ITU-R P.2040 to conductivity priors for Sionna's gradient descent on accumulated received signal strength (RSS) measurements; waypoint planning selects the next measurement location online using residual RSS calibration error and image coverage. In a real indoor scenario, the framework achieves a normalized mean absolute conductivity error of 1.74 × 10-4 within 20 m of travel; random initialization never converges, while random waypoints require over twice the travel.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: A Comparative Evaluation of Modbus Security Telemetry Extraction.
abstract: Network security frequently treats packet captures as ground truth, although most detection and analysis pipelines operate on structured telemetry produced by protocol parsers rather than directly on packet bytes. This study evaluates how parser selection affects Modbus telemetry by processing an identical controlled traffic with Suricata, TShark, and Zeek. Their outputs are compared in terms of output structure, protocol-field fidelity, payload visibility, transaction reconstruction, exception representation, and timing observability. The results show differences in both record structure and analytical content. Consequently, the selected parser determines which features are directly available for detection engineering, behavioral analysis, SIEM integration, dataset construction, and machine-learning applications. These findings show that protocol parsing is not a neutral preprocessing step. Even with identical packet-level input, parser implementation and configuration can alter the structure, completeness, and semantics of the resulting cybersecurity dataset. Reproducible industrial cybersecurity research should therefore document and validate the parsing stage and use cross-parser verification when feasible.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Federated Transfer Learning with Attentional Graph Neural Networks for Zero-Day IoT Botnet Detection and Secure Edge Orchestration.
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) devices are increasingly appearing in a wide variety of edge environments, and these environments have become cybersecurity hot spots due to the increased vulnerability of them to sophisticated Zero-Day botnets propagation and Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks. However, traditional centralized intrusion detection system (IDS) is not capable of dealing with privacy constraints, communication overhead and dynamic topological structures of modern IoT networks. To solve these problems, a novel federated transfer learning framework, with the support of Attentional Graph Neural Networks (AGNN) is proposed for decentralized zero-day botnet detection at resource-constrained edge nodes. Proposed architecture includes federated learning to achieve collaborative model training, without sharing raw telemetry data and graph-based spatial modeling for capturing complex inter-device communication anomalies. Moreover, a transfer learning mechanism fine-tunes pre-trained threat intelligence on newly emerging edge sub-networks with limited fine-tuning. Empirical results on the benchmark IoT intrusion datasets (N-BaIoT and BoT-IoT) show a detection accuracy of 98.6%, 0.97 in ROC-AUC, a reduction of false alarm rate to 0.42% and a reduction of communication bandwidth overhead of 45.3% when compared to the traditional centralized deep learning paradigms. The results of ablation experiments indicate that the base GNN, the base GNN with attention and the base GNN with federated attention, together with the full transfer-learning setup, gradually improves the ablation results.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: RAMP: History-Aware Multi-Access Path Management for Resilient Edge Networks.
abstract: Multi-access connectivity can improve the resilience of mission-critical edge services by allowing traffic to migrate across heterogeneous network paths. However, conventional path-selection policies typically react to current availability or measured performance. In recurrently unstable networks, a degraded path may briefly appear healthy and attract traffic again before its condition has stabilized. Such premature path reuse can cause repeated path migration, tail-latency spikes, and deadline violations. This paper presents RAMP, a lightweight history-aware multi-access path-management policy designed for recurrent network degradation and recovery. RAMP combines exponentially smoothed round-trip-time (RTT) measurements with short-term indicators of instability, including recent failures, consecutive failures, and latency variability. Recently unstable paths therefore retain a temporary risk penalty even after their instantaneous latency improves. We evaluate RAMP against single-path operation, reactive failover, minimum-RTT selection, and a hysteresis-based RTT baseline across five controlled network conditions. The evaluation comprises 75 independent 60-second runs and 9,000 application transactions. Under recurrent degradation and recovery, RAMP achieves 99.72% deadline satisfaction, compared with 98.61% for MinRTT and 94.44% for hysteresis-based RTT selection. RAMP reduces scheduler switches from six to two and Resilience Debt from 3.33 s to 0.17 s relative to the hysteresis baseline. Under bursty impairment, RAMP again reaches 99.72% deadline satisfaction and 0.17 s Resilience Debt. Conversely, under stable, monotonic-degradation, and hard-failure conditions, its advantage is small or absent. The results show that short-term instability memory is particularly useful under recurrent non-stationary impairment, where instantaneous path quality can encourage premature path reuse.

title: Poster: From Live Camera Streams to Continuously Updated Urban 3D Models at the 6G Edge.
abstract: This poster examines the challenges of constructing and continuously updating radiance-field models of urban environments from live video streams generated by roadside and vehicle-mounted cameras. Using data from the CARLA simulator, we present preliminary results on the feasibility of a reconstruction pipeline supported by a representative 6G edge-cloud infrastructure and investigate how existing models adapt as new observations become available.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Toward Edge-Assisted Live Synthesis of 3D Digital Twins in 6G.
abstract: Live synthesis of 3D digital twins from vehicle-mounted and roadside camera streams could provide timely, spatially rich representations of urban environments. However, constructing radiance-field models from distributed camera streams with short processing delays introduces substantial computation, coordination, and localization requirements. This paper presents a controlled measurement study of centralized, distributed, and federated radiance-field synthesis under prospective 6G edge-cloud assumptions. Using a CARLA-based vehicular scenario, we show that centralized model training can reach the target reconstruction quality in under 2 minutes under favorable configurations, excluding data transfer and method-specific preprocessing. Distributed and federated approaches spread the training workload across edge nodes: Mega-NeRF enables fast model merging but achieves lower quality than centralized Nerfacto, whereas Fed3DGS approaches centralized Splatfacto quality on guided trajectories but becomes aggregation-bound. Moderate camera-position errors cause limited degradation, whereas multi-meter errors substantially reduce reconstruction quality. These results identify faster model synthesis, efficient aggregation, coverage-aware data acquisition, and accurate localization as key requirements for scalable live synthesis of 3D digital twins.
