title: PRISM: Reinforced Semantic Communication for Decentralized Federated Anomaly Detection in Vehicular Networks.
abstract: Decentralized Federated Learning (DFL) enables collaborative learning that preserves privacy, but faces critical communication challenges in bandwidth-constrained environments such as vehicular networks. We propose Policy-driven Representation and Information Selection Method (PRISM), a Reinforcement Learning (RL)-based method that optimizes semantic communication in DFL through adaptive representation selection and intelligent topology management. Our dual-model architecture separates task learning (autoencoder-based anomaly detection) from communication control (Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based decision making), enabling agents to dynamically select between transmitting full model weights or compressed trajectory embeddings. We formulate this as a Decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (Dec-POMDP) and train using a Centralized Training Decentralized Execution (CTDE) paradigm. We demonstrate our method through a digital twin monitoring scenario where vehicles collaboratively detect trajectory anomalies in neighbors' behavior in real time, and the logged detections support forensic analysis, insurance claims, and fleet auditing. Experiments on Simulation of Urban Mobility (SUMO) generated Barcelona traffic data show an F1-score of 0.90, scaling from 2 to 128 agents with graceful degradation past N = 32, Byzantine-robust aggregation, and validation on Next Generation Simulation (NGSIM) US-101 real traces (F1 0.82). The learned policy exhibits emergent temporal behavior: transmitting weights early during training when model divergence is high, then shifting to embeddings as models converge, with the weight-to-embedding mix derived as the equilibrium of the communication budget constraint. The method generalizes to other bandwidth-limited collaborative learning domains.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: METRO: MAP-Enhanced Twin Rollouts for Reinforcement Learning-Based Coverage and Capacity Optimization.
abstract: Few-shot coverage and capacity optimization (CCO) under a small adjustment budget is challenging: model-based methods suffer from simulator mismatch, while feedback-based methods are sample-starved. We address this challenge with a rollout-based policy-improvement framework. Rather than deploying the trained policy's highest-probability action directly, we use the policy as a proposal mechanism and a maximum a posteriori (MAP)-calibrated digital twin (DT) as the evaluator. The policy samples candidate actions; each is simulated for multiple steps inside the twin, and only the highest-return candidate is deployed. Sparse measurements report signal strength and quality but not user-equipment (UE) locations; we therefore estimate UE locations by MAP inference using DT-predicted measurements as likelihoods and recalibrate the DT to the current network state at each step. Three trainingside components strengthen the candidate generation: a Heaviside reward for safety, a recurrent network for partial observability, and domain randomization for simulator mismatch. Ablation studies validate these components. Under a 10-shot emulated-field budget, METRO achieves a lower violation rate than classical simulated annealing and gains comparable to a 50×-budget baseline.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Optimal Parallel Scheduling under Concave Speedup Functions.
abstract: Efficiently scheduling parallel computing resources across multiple concurrent jobs is a core challenge in modern cloud and edge computing systems that support AI-driven applications. Allocating more resources to a job accelerates its completion, but with diminishing returns. Prior work (heSRPT) has solved this problem for certain speedup functions with an exponential form, providing a closed-form solution. However, the general case with arbitrary concave speedup functions—which more accurately capture real-world workloads—has remained open. In this paper, we solve this open problem by developing optimal scheduling algorithms for parallel jobs under general concave speedup functions. We first discover a fundamental and broadly-applicable rule for optimal parallel scheduling, namely the Consistent Derivative Ratio (CDR) Rule , which states that the ratio of the derivatives of the speedup functions across active jobs remains constant over time. To efficiently compute the optimal allocations that satisfy the CDR Rule, we propose the General Water-Filling (GWF) method, a more general version of classical water-filling in wireless communications. Combining these insights, we design the SmartFill Algorithm to solve the general scheduling problem. Unlike heSRPT, which always allocates resources to all active jobs, SmartFill selectively determines which jobs should receive resources and how much they should be allocated. For a broad class of so-called regular speedup functions, SmartFill yields closed-form optimal solutions, while for non-regular functions it efficiently computes the optimum numerically. Simulation results show that SmartFill can outperform heSRPT across a wide range of concave speedup functions.

title: POLAR: Online Learning for LoRA Adapter Caching and Routing in Edge LLM Serving.
abstract: Edge deployment of large language models (LLMs) increasingly relies on libraries of lightweight LoRA adapters, yet GPU/DRAM can keep only a small resident subset at a time. Serving a request through a non-resident adapter requires paging its weights from storage, incurring measurable latency. This creates a two-timescale online control problem: on a slow timescale, the system selects which adapters remain resident in fast memory, while on a fast timescale it routes each request to an adapter whose context-dependent utility is unknown a priori. The two decisions are tightly coupled: the cache determines the cost of exploration, and the router determines which adapters receive informative feedback. We formulate this joint caching-and-routing problem as a two-timescale contextual bandit and propose POLAR (Paging and Online Learning for Adapter Routing). POLAR pairs a cache-aware LinUCB router with an epoch-based cache controller. We study two variants. A fixed-epoch version provides a robust baseline with worst-case regret guarantees under arbitrary contexts. An epoch-doubling version, POLAR+, adds forced exploration and improved cache optimization to achieve O~(dNT+KT) sublinear regret under stochastic regularity and cacheability conditions, where N is the adapter count, K the cache size, d the context dimension, and T the horizon. The routing term matches the standard contextual-bandit rate up to logarithmic factors, showing that the memory hierarchy does not fundamentally slow routing learning. Experiments using 15 real LoRA adapters for Qwen2.5-7B together with measured GPU paging latencies show that adaptive cache control substantially outperforms heuristic caching baselines.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Demo: Closed-Loop Sionna-Isaac Sim Co-Simulation Framework for Wireless-Aware Robot Navigation over ROS 2.
abstract: A robot that offloads its control loop to the network carries the receiver with it, so link quality is decided by where it goes. Simulating this requires both a physics engine and a site-specific propagation model at once; to our knowledge no simulator natively unifies both, with existing couplings of the two limited to offline analyses. We demonstrate a real-time co-simulation framework coupling NVIDIA Isaac Sim and NVIDIA Sionna over ROS 2 that closes the perception-action-communication (PAC) loop between them. Sionna ray-traces the base-station-to-robot channel over the exact geometry Isaac Sim simulates on—rather than modeling it stochastically—and feeds channel states back into the control loop in real time. Ray-traced on GPU, the coverage map is refreshed in ~16 ms (~60 Hz), fast enough for real-time control. To showcase the framework's utility, we implement a wireless-aware navigation application in an OpenStreetMap(OSM)-derived SUTD campus twin with two Nova Carter robots: the closed-loop planner eliminates communication outage at only +7.4% traversal time over the shortest-path baseline (which spends 7.9 s of its 81.2 s run disconnected).
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Distributed Collaborative Positioning through ISAC for GPS-Denied Robotic Swarms.
abstract: Robotic swarms in GPS-denied environments require accurate position and velocity in real-time for all nodes, without external infrastructure or centralized control. Existing positioning approaches, including collaborative positioning, fail because of non-scalable (O(N2)) measurement overhead or centralized architectures that cannot keep pace with high-mobility swarms. We present DiCoP, a novel paradigm of Distributed Collaborative Positioning through asynchronous, multi-static ISAC. Each node broadcasts a lightweight ISAC waveform, enabling all neighbors to passively and asynchronously measure relative distances and Doppler shifts through a novel differential sensing technique that cancels clock and channel frequency offsets with only O(1) overhead. Coupled with a novel joint distance-velocity localization, each node independently estimates its position and velocity, alleviating topology rigidity requirements of conventional distance-based methods. A sensing-aware distributed MAC further prioritizes measurements from fast-moving, under-measured nodes to accelerate convergence. Evaluated on our UGV swarm prototype, as well as NS3 simulations for large-scale UAV swarms (up to 100 UAVs at 15 m/s), DiCoP achieves sub-2 m error for over 89.38% of estimates, 0.062 m/s velocity error, and 54.3 ms convergence time, outperforming GPS, IMU, WiFi FTM, and centralized baselines while maintaining stable accuracy over extended mission duration.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Learning When to Update: A Near-Optimal Timing Bandit Approach.
abstract: Systems operating in dynamic environments require timely updates to sustain performance. For resource-intensive systems such as machine learning models and digital twins, strategically timing updates is essential. Updating too frequently wastes resources, while updating too infrequently leads to costly performance degradation. The problem is particularly challenging when the system's degradation pattern is unknown a priori, as is common in new operating environments. We formalize this challenge as a novel timing bandit problem, where each arm represents a candidate update interval with a fixed update cost and an unknown, stochastic degradation cost. Three structural properties distinguish this setting from standard multi-armed bandits: selecting an interval commits the learner to multiple time slots before the next update; arm costs are composed of per-step degradation costs and a fixed update cost; and selecting a longer interval naturally reveals degradation at every intermediate step, providing consecutive feedback relevant to shorter intervals. By exploiting these structures, we develop Balanced Consecutive Arm Elimination (BCAE). BCAE achieves O~(T) regret, improving upon the Ω~(KT) regret of standard bandit algorithms in this setting, where K is the number of candidate update intervals. We further propose an Optimism-Enhanced variant (OE-BCAE) that integrates lower-confidence-bound principles to improve empirical adaptivity while preserving the same regret order. Moreover, the regret bound achieved by our algorithms matches the theoretical lower bound up to logarithmic factors. Simulation results demonstrate that our algorithms achieve low regret and remain stable as both the number of arms and the update cost vary.

title: Receiver-Aware Token Routing for Semantic Communication.
abstract: Mission-critical mobile networks increasingly support AI-enabled services under heterogeneous and degraded wireless conditions. Semantic communication offers a promising approach by transmitting compact task-relevant representations, but most existing methods remain receiver-agnostic. We propose a receiver-aware semantic routing framework that combines hard receiver-conditioned token gating with learned mixture-of-experts transformation. A shared Vision Transformer extracts patch-level tokens, while a receiver-conditioned router jointly produces token-selection scores and expert-routing logits. Hard Top-K gating determines which routed token representations contribute to semantic aggregation, and soft expert routing adapts token representations to the receiver profile. Experiments on the MS COCO multi-label recognition task under high-SNR, low-SNR, and constrained token-retention conditions show consistent gains over static conditioning, random token selection, and pruning baselines. The results demonstrate that jointly controlling token retention and receiver-aware semantic transformation improves semantic inference under the evaluated AWGN and token-retention conditions.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Decision-Focused Learning for Bidding Optimization in Online Advertising.
abstract: In large-scale networked systems such as online marketplaces and advertising exchanges, real-time decision-making under dynamic environments is a fundamental challenge. A widely adopted paradigm is the predict-then-optimize workflow, where the prediction stage estimates key factors for decisions, and the optimization stage optimizes objectives based on these factors. However, existing prediction models are typically trained only for prediction accuracy, without awareness of the downstream optimization objective, leading to suboptimal results. We investigate this problem in the context of first-price auction bidding, a canonical decision problem in networked platforms. Specifically, we first propose the Decision-Focused Bidding (DFB) approach, which retains the predict-then-optimize workflow, but integrates the downstream objective into the training of the prediction model. To overcome the zero-gradient issue in back-propagation, we develop a smoothed decision mapping that provides usable gradients while preserving clear interpretability in the bidding context. We further show that DFB's decision-learning objective and the classical objective of learning winning probabilities are complementary under non-i.i.d. environments, and accordingly propose Enhanced DFB (EDFB), which jointly optimizes both objectives to achieve robust generalization in real-world bidding environments. Finally, our EDFB approach has been deployed in a production auto-bidding system, where it achieves a 2.3% GMV lift in a 3-day online A/B test over about 100 billion requests.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Query-Aware Temporal Evidence Prefetching to Support Communication-Efficient Video AIoT Reasoning.
abstract: Video Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) systems increasingly use vision-language models (VLMs) to answer questions about dynamic scenes, yet continuous high-resolution streaming may exceed wireless and latency budgets. We therefore study a layered setting in which the receiver always holds a low-resolution stream and requests only a limited number of high-resolution enhancement patches. Within this setting, we propose query-aware temporal semantic prefetching (QTPF), which uses the task query and prior low-resolution images to predict evidence locations in the next sampled observation before it arrives. On 14,913 LingoQA scenery questions, QTPF obtains 0.6355 Recall@5 under an OpenCLIP evidence target, compared with 0.5858 for a query-only learned model and 0.6270 for an independently trained query-aware last-frame predictor. The advantage persists under independently generated SigLIP targets, where QTPF obtains 0.5473 against 0.5328 for the last-frame predictor. With five enhancement patches, the delivered JPEG payload averages 9.77 KB, which is 20.9% below the 12.35 KB full-resolution image, and the predictor adds only 0.75 ms on an RTX 6000 Ada GPU.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Reusable Resource Allocation under Adversarial Arrivals: Learning with Delayed Feedback.
abstract: We study an online reusable resource allocation problem motivated by mobile edge AI platforms, where sequentially arriving requests must be immediately admitted and assigned to one of multiple edge service options with limited reusable capacities or offloaded to a remote central server. If accepted, a request occupies one service slot of the selected option for a random duration and yields a stochastic reward. The problem is particularly challenging because arrivals may be adversarial, reward and service-time statistics are both unknown and heterogeneous across request types and service options, and reward feedback can be delayed beyond service completion. To address these challenges, we propose an index-based online learning algorithm that combines optimistic reward estimates with a conservative, utilization-aware opportunity-cost penalty that captures the future value of reusable capacity. Using a primal-dual framework built on a novel reverse-order benchmark, we establish competitive-ratio guarantees under both bounded and light-tailed unbounded feedback delays. In particular, under a homogeneous reward-service model with i.i.d. inter-arrival times, our algorithm achieves an asymptotic competitive ratio of 1 - 1/e as reusable capacities grow large. Experimental results on a real-world dataset further demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Joint Incentive Contract and Assignment Design for Mobile Networked Platforms with Endogenous Supply.
abstract: Mobile networked platforms such as crowdsensing markets, edge-computing exchanges, vehicular service systems, and sponsored-content programs must coordinate two coupled levers: an assignment rule that decides who serves each request and an incentive contract that determines how realized value is shared. In all four settings, supply is endogenous, that is, it depends on the platform's own decisions: providers remain active only when expected earnings cover their private participation cost. We study a discounted platform problem in which assignment and revenue sharing jointly shape future supply. We calibrate the tractable one-period objective using an auxiliary memoryless discounted surrogate: it maximizes a global lower bound on that surrogate objective, and near high-survival stationary operating points its retention coefficient becomes the local shadow price of discounted future welfare within the surrogate model. This yields an Equimarginal Principle requiring efficient platforms to equalize the marginal retention efficiency of assignment and contracting. Under complete information, we obtain an urgency-adjusted assignment score, a KKT condition for the contract, and a Frank-Wolfe coordinate-ascent benchmark with an O(t/K) joint stationarity rate. Under hidden provider quality, we develop SE-RW-UCB, a subsidized-exploration algorithm with retention-weighted contextual assignment and a learned safe contract floor. A KuaiRec-based online recommendation benchmark shows that separated designs leave a sizable retention gap. In that benchmark, Oracle Fixed is the profit leader, whereas SE-RW-UCB attains the strongest high-type and all-provider retention at an interior contract. The service-quality differences are comparatively small, indicating that the main leverage of co-design in this calibration lies in supply preservation rather than per-request quality gains.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: LLM-Enabled Self-Organizing UAV Networks for Autonomous Service Provisioning.
abstract: The growing demand for flexible and resilient low-altitude connectivity is driving UAV networks toward increasingly autonomous operation. However, existing approaches often assume known user distributions, fixed network configurations, or treat exploration, access, and backhaul separately, resulting in a gap between user discovery and end-to-end service in initially unknown environments. To address this challenge, we propose a self-organizing heterogeneous UAV networking framework, referred to as Discovery-to-Service (D2S) Network, that supports the complete process from user discovery to end-to-end service provisioning. The framework adopts a dual-timescale coordination mechanism: at the fast timescale, onboard graph reinforcement learning agents perform user exploration and local control, while at the slower timescale, a basestation-hosted LLM reconfigures the access and backhaul infrastructure based on discovered demands and the global network state. Experiments over 42 scenarios show that, compared with a heuristic connectivity-constrained grid-greedy method, the proposed framework improves effective coverage by 23.38 percentage points, terminal throughput by 55.3%, and cumulative throughput by 44.3%, demonstrating its effectiveness for autonomous network formation under unknown demand.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Pushing Bistatic Wireless Sensing toward High Accuracy at the Sub-Wavelength Scale.
abstract: Contactless sensing using wireless communication signals has garnered significant attention due to its non-intrusive nature and ubiquitous infrastructure. Despite the promise, the inherent bistatic deployment of wireless communication introduces clock asynchronism, which leads to unknown phase offsets in channel response and hinders fine-grained sensing. State-of-the-art systems widely adopt the cross-antenna channel response ratio to cancel these detrimental phase offsets. However, the channel response ratio preserves sensing feature accuracy only at integer-wavelength target displacements, losing sub-wavelength fidelity. To overcome this limitation, we derive the first quantitative mapping between the distorted ratio feature and the ideal-channel sensing feature. Building on this foundation, we develop a robust framework that leverages raw channel response amplitude to recover the ideal sensing feature from the distorted ratio. Real-world experiments across Wi-Fi and LoRa signals demonstrate that our method can effectively reconstruct sub-wavelength displacement details, achieving nearly an order-of-magnitude improvement in accuracy.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Age of Information for Real-Time Radio Map Monitoring.
abstract: In this paper, we propose radio map age of information (RM-AOI), a new metric for measuring the information freshness of a reconstructed radio map. Specifically, we consider a radio map monitoring system in which sensors transmit spectrum measurement packets to a central monitoring station for radio map reconstruction. To reflect the contributions of measurements to radio map reconstruction, we define RM-AOI by weighting each sensor's age of information (AoI). We model packet generation and transmission as a homogeneous multi-source M/M/1 first-come-first-served (FCFS) queue. Under this model, we develop an analytical framework based on time reversal and joint workload analysis to derive exact expressions for the time average and temporal variance of RM-AOI. Simulations validate the exact expressions, demonstrate how queue parameters affect RM-AOI, and show that the mean squared error (MSE) of radio map reconstruction generally increases with both metrics.

title: TrustSense: Structure-Adaptive Trust Inference for Resilient Cooperative IoT Sensing.
abstract: Cooperative IoT sensing must assess reports from noisy, faulty, or compromised devices despite churn and changing inter-device relationships. We present TrustSense, a structure-adaptive GNN framework for per-report trust evaluation. TrustSense represents active devices as a dynamic graph and maps each report's neighborhood-based reconstruction residual to a trust score. A layer-wise soft edge mask downweights less informative dependencies, while forced anchor attention reserves a controlled share of attention for available trusted anchors. At runtime, historical consistency drives anchor-rooted credit diffusion to prioritize returning devices, and accepted reports guide subsequent evaluations. Shared GNN parameters make TrustSense inductive, enabling targeted adaptation to unseen devices without usable history. TrustSense is also location-centric, device-agnostic, and prior-free with respect to the sensing process, assuming neither a parametric sensing-value distribution nor a known propagation model. We evaluate TrustSense on synthetic RF data and real LoED traces with injected attacks. With 10% additive-bias attackers on LoED, it improves F1 by 4.25× over the strongest evaluated baseline and achieves a lower Brier score. These gains persist with up to 50% malicious devices, while inference latency remains within 230-250 ms at several thousand devices.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: PQ-FL-IDS: A Post Quantum Safe Federated Edge Intrusion Detection Scheme underlying 6G.
abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables Intrusion Detection System (IDS) models to be trained across Sixth Generation (6G) edge nodes without transferring sensitive traffic records to a central server. However, the model updates exchanged during FL-based IDS (FL-IDS) training remain exposed to interception and harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks by quantum-capable adversaries. This paper presents PQ-FL-IDS, a post-quantum (PQ) FL-IDS scheme for 6G edge networks. It protects model-update exchange using a real, non-simulated Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism (ML-KEM-512, NIST FIPS 203), the Advanced Encryption Standard in Galois/Counter Mode with a 256-bit key (AES-256-GCM), and per-round forward secrecy through ephemeral key pairs. Differentially Private Stochastic Gradient Descent (DP-SGD) with Rényi DP accounting further bounds record-level leakage from local updates. In each round, clients train locally with calibrated DP noise, encrypt the model update, and send only the protected payload for server-side aggregation. We evaluate PQ-FL-IDS on ToN-IoT with a 1D-CNN and FedAvg, and on CICIoT2023 with MobileNetV2-1D and FedProx, under baseline, PQC-only, and PQC+DP settings. ML-KEM-512 with AES-256-GCM adds less than 0.003% computational overhead relative to per-round training time and at most 3.5 KB of payload expansion, with no accuracy loss, and remains stable from 2 to 5 clients. The privacy analysis shows predictable ε growth with the subsampling rate and characterizes the privacy-utility frontier: formal budgets of ε = 0.9-2.4 are obtained for σ = 0.8-1.1, with a utility cost that depends strongly on task complexity.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: TWINERGY: Digital Twin Empowered Practical Energy Saving in Heterogeneous Mobile Networks.
abstract: Energy consumption has become a pressing concern as mobile networks expand rapidly, with the radio access network accounting for the dominant share. Among energy-saving techniques, cell shutdown offers large saving potential: it selectively switches off capacity cells in heterogeneous networks while a coverage layer preserves service. However, optimizing cell shutdown policies faces two key challenges: (i) live trial-and-error is prohibitively risky, while traditional simulators cannot capture the complex dynamics needed for reliable evaluation; (ii) operator-deployed threshold policies are interpretable but hard to optimize at scale. On the other hand, binary status optimization is more tractable but produces policies incompatible with operator workflows. We propose Twinergy, a digital twin-empowered framework for practical cell shutdown at scale. Twinergy builds a Network Digital Twin for safe virtual evaluation, and decouples policy design into two stages: first optimizing binary on/off decisions under QoS constraints, and then mapping them into deployable thresholds, with a dedicated module for each. For scalable decision optimization, we design Cable, a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework with shared policies, causal graph-based spatio-temporal encoding, and credit-guided cooperative learning. For threshold synthesis, we design a differentiable mapping module that introduces SoftControl as a surrogate for hard dual-threshold logic, enabling thresholds to be calibrated in continuous space via stable supervised optimization. Experiments on a digital twin built from 14,349 real-world base stations and deployments across three commercial trial networks with over 3,400 cells show that Twinergy achieves up to 26.0% and 12.4% energy savings in 4G and 5G digital-twin evaluation, respectively, and delivers up to 13.07% and 12.20% energy-efficiency improvements in rural and dense 5G live networks without degrading QoS.

title: FedCRA: Client Risk-aware Aggregation via Update Reconstruction for IoT-based Federated Learning.
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables distributed model training without sharing raw data, making it particularly suitable for Internet of Things (IoT) environments. However, FL remains vulnerable to poisoning attacks, where malicious clients manipulate local updates to corrupt global model optimization. Existing defenses mainly focus on updates within a single round and may confuse heterogeneous benign updates with malicious ones. In this paper, we propose FedCRA, a client risk-aware aggregation framework that exploits historical trajectories and trusted reference updates to reconstruct updates. Furthermore, the risk-aware aggregation jointly considers reconstruction gap, reference gap, and historical trajectory information to adaptively suppress suspicious updates. Extensive experiments under multiple poisoning attacks and heterogeneous data distributions demonstrate that FedCRA achieves stronger robustness than several representative aggregation methods while maintaining good scalability in large-scale FL.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Poster: Jamming-Resilient FR3 5G NR via Adaptive Sensing and Covariance-Based RX Null-Forming.
abstract: We present work in progress on interference rejection at a software-defined 5G NR gNB through receive-side null-forming, where the spatial covariance matrix used to compute the null-forming weights is estimated exclusively from transmission-free windows, with neither gNB nor UE signals present. Silent sensing opportunities arise during light DL traffic or are explicitly reserved within the TDD pattern. A power detector on the gNB's own receive chain identifies these windows in real time from ADC energy, allowing the FPGA to select exactly the samples that are free of the gNB's own transmission for covariance estimation. The resulting null-forming weights suppress an interferer without attenuating the desired uplink. The system is implemented on an Open Air Interface (OAI) 5G NR standalone testbed with an FPGA/RFSoC-based FR3 multi-antenna front-end and a software-defined incumbent/jammer emulator.

title: C-MoA-XRT: Explainability-Aware Trust Routing for Collaborative Threat Detection in Mobile-Edge Networks.
abstract: Threat detection in mobile-edge networks requires reliable inference from heterogeneous telemetry whose availability and evidential quality may vary over time. LLM-assisted detectors further introduce uncertainty because prediction confidence may not reflect evidence trustworthiness, while collaborative reasoning can amplify unsupported decisions. This paper proposes C-MoA-XRT, a trust-aware collaborative Mixture-of-Agents framework for resilient mobile-edge threat detection. C-MoA-XRT distributes complementary network evidence across specialized LLM agents and performs event-specific trust routing before collaborative inference. The proposed routing mechanism separates prediction confidence from decision authority by assessing the reliability, consistency, and evidential support of each specialist output. A defensive red-team reasoning stage subsequently examines the fused evidence, while an evidence-anchored decision firewall constrains unstable collaborative reasoning from overriding the calibrated detection outcome. Experiments on NF-UNSW-NB15 show that C-MoA-XRT achieves an F1 score of 0.900 with full attack recall and reduces the false-positive rate by approximately 75% relative to the evaluated single-agent RAG+LLM baseline. Under measurement drift, trust-aware evidence gating improves PR-AUC from 0.694 to 0.917 over confidence-based routing, while maintaining resilience under the evaluated telemetry-dropout and unreliable-specialist conditions. These results demonstrate that explicit control of evidence trust and reasoning authority can improve the robustness of collaborative LLM-based threat detection in mobile-edge networks.

title: Optimizing Stochastic Gradient Push under Broadcast Communications.
abstract: We consider the problem of minimizing the convergence time for decentralized federated learning (DFL) in wireless networks under broadcast communications, with focus on mixing matrix design. The mixing matrix is a critical hyperparameter for DFL that simultaneously controls the convergence rate across iterations and the communication demand per iteration, both strongly influencing the convergence time. Although the problem has been studied previously, existing solutions are mostly designed for decentralized parallel stochastic gradient descent (D-PSGD), which requires the mixing matrix to be symmetric and doubly stochastic. These constraints confine the activated communication graph to undirected (i.e., bidirected) graphs, which limits design flexibility. In contrast, we consider mixing matrix design for stochastic gradient push (SGP), which allows asymmetric mixing matrices and hence directed communication graphs. By analyzing how the convergence rate of SGP depends on the mixing matrices, we extract an objective function that explicitly depends on graph-theoretic parameters of the activated communication graph, based on which we develop an efficient design algorithm with performance guarantees. Our evaluations based on real data show that the proposed solution can notably reduce the convergence time compared to the state of the art without compromising the quality of the trained model.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: FEdgeNAV: Edge-Based Federated Learning Framework for Wheel Odometry Fault Detection in Industrial AGV Fleet Navigation.
abstract: Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs) rely on accurate wheel odometry for reliable navigation; however, wheel slip and varying terrain conditions introduce positioning errors that degrade navigation performance. This paper presents FEdgeNAV, a lightweight edge-based federated learning framework for collaborative wheel odometry fault detection in heterogeneous industrial environments. The proposed framework employs a lightweight 1D CNN-GRU model trained collaboratively across distributed edge clients using Federated Averaging (FedAvg), while keeping raw navigation data local by exchanging only model parameters. Wheel odometry faults are identified through residual analysis between the estimated and measured vehicle speeds. Experimental evaluation on the NavINST dataset demonstrated accurate vehicle-speed estimation and residual-based wheel-odometry fault detection across heterogeneous operating conditions. Furthermore, the proposed framework achieved computationally efficient inference on the NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano, demonstrating its suitability for real-time deployment on resource-constrained edge platforms for industrial AGVs.
