title: Foundation Model-Aided Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Wireless Random Access Network Optimization.
abstract: Random access (RA) is one of the most foundational medium access control (MAC) layer scheduling schemes for handling unpredictable data traffic from multiple terminals. While multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) has been explored to optimize RA-based wireless networks, its reliance on experience-driven, distributed policy learning incurs significant training overhead for each optimization task, limiting its feasibility in real-world applications. In this work, we propose to leverage a foundation model (FM) to improve MARL efficiency across diverse RA network optimization tasks. Specifically, we design an FM-aided actor-critic algorithm within a consensus-based decentralized MARL architecture and provide its convergence analysis under local reward exchanges and nonlinear value function approximations to show that our algorithm achieves the same convergence order as the conventional MARL with critic model exchanges and linear approximations. Our numerical results show that our FM-based approach significantly enhances MARL speed for RA network optimization.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Towards Agile and Active Scene Update for Embodied Space Exploration: A WiFi-Guided Approach.
abstract: Timely scene updating is essential for embodied agents operating in dynamic indoor environments. While cameras and LiDAR are effective for high-fidelity reconstruction and verification, relying on them alone for long-term maintenance is costly, since robots must repeatedly revisit large areas to rediscover relatively sparse changes. This paper presents WiDR, a WiFi-guided framework for efficient and active scene updating. The key idea is to use ubiquitous wireless signals as a low-overhead prior indicating where meaningful changes are likely to occur, thereby guiding visual or depth-based verification, rather than using wireless sensing to reconstruct the scene itself. WiDR integrates wireless priors with floorplan context to build a belief-aware navigation graph, and formulates scene updating as a budget-constrained utility maximization problem that jointly considers navigation, sensing, updating, and model refinement. To remain effective in long-term dynamic environments, WiDR further incorporates active refinement using robot-verified observations to improve its change prediction quality. Experimental results in a three-room indoor testbed show that WiDR achieves higher update utility under the same budget by directing sensing effort toward high-value regions instead of relying on coverage-driven or vision-only exploration.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Prism: Communication-efficient Distributed Inference for Foundation Models at Edge.
abstract: Foundation models (FMs) achieved remarkable success across vision and language tasks but pose significant challenges for deployment at the edge devices. This motivates the need for practical and efficient strategies for distributed inference at the edge. In this work, we propose Prism, a communication-efficient and compute-aware strategy for distributed Transformer inference. Prism leverages a Segment Means representation to approximate intermediate features, substantially reducing inter-device communication. Additionally, we restructure the self-attention to eliminate redundant computations caused by per-device Key/Value calculation in position-wise partitioning and design a partition-aware causal masking scheme tailored for autoregressive models. We evaluate Prism on ViT, BERT, and GPT-2 across diverse datasets, namely CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet-1k, GLUE, and CBT. Our results demonstrate substantial reductions in communication overhead (up to 99.2% for BERT at compression rate CR = 128) and per-device computation (51.24% for BERT at the same setting), with only minor accuracy degradation. This method offers a scalable and practical solution for deploying foundation models in distributed resource-constrained environments.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: MIRA: An Edge-Cloud Multimodal LLM Framework for DESH Assessment in IoT-Enabled MRI Workflows.
abstract: Connected MRI scanners operate as networked medical devices within DICOM-based healthcare Internet of Things (IoT) workflows, but conventional connectivity primarily moves images to a Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS) rather than adding task-specific reasoning near acquisition. Building on DESH-App 2.0, a preceding machine-learning contribution accepted for oral presentation at SIN Firenze 2026, this paper specifies MIRA (Multimodal Imaging Reasoning and Assessment), a vendor-neutral edge-cloud module for assessing disproportionately enlarged subarachnoid spaces (DESH). A hospital-edge gateway validates and de-identifies 3D T1-weighted DICOM studies, derives ventricular, high-convexity, and Sylvian-fissure masks with SegFormer3D, and converts each volume into a compact evidence package comprising 12 representative slices with overlays, 17 global, zonal, and ratio features, and quality-control tokens. LLaVA-Med-7B and Lingshu-7B are adapted through 4-bit QLoRA to return constrained JSON containing class, confidence, named anatomical evidence, and an abstention or quality warning. The edge-cloud partition keeps raw volumes inside the institutional network; only the compact evidence package may reach an authenticated inference service, while structured outputs return to the PACS workstation. The evaluation protocol jointly covers diagnostic discrimination, calibration, evidence agreement, unsupported claims, abstention, latency, transmitted bytes, memory demand, link-loss recovery, and multi-device interoperability. MIRA is designed to add auditable multimodal reasoning to connected MRI workflows without modifying safety-critical scanner controls.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: An Agentic AI Architecture for Zero-Touch IoT Device Onboarding and Interoperability.
abstract: The heterogeneity of Internet of Things (IoT) devices remains a major barrier to scalable deployment, automated onboarding, and cross-platform interoperability. Device-specific protocols, software dependencies, telemetry formats, and runtime constraints often require manual configuration and ad-hoc integration logic. This paper proposes an agentic AI architecture for zero-touch IoT device onboarding, where a large language model is used as an autonomous configuration agent capable of generating device-side software, installing dependencies, validating runtime behavior, and recursively correcting failures until convergence is achieved. The proposed architecture introduces a closed-loop workflow that combines device inspection, AI-based runtime generation, remote deployment, telemetry validation, and self-correction. Interoperability is addressed through a normalized telemetry contract that abstracts device-specific behavior into a common telemetry representation. We evaluate the approach on a real IoT device by benchmarking multiple AI models under clean installation conditions in two campaigns: the original pipeline and a second pipeline assisted by a locally trained semantic context optimizer. The comparison covers convergence time, correction cycles, recursive iterations, and prompt tokens. The optimizer-assisted campaign reduced prompt redundancy and recursive recovery effort while preserving successful onboarding across all tested models. Overall, the results show that agentic AI can support zero-touch onboarding while exposing measurable differences among models in reliability, efficiency, and runtime convergence.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Routing and Topology Design for Low Earth Orbit Satellite Networks under Demand Uncertainty.
abstract: We study the space segment of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks that support satellite-to-satellite communication via inter-satellite links (ISLs). Our goal is to jointly design topologies and routing strategies that are robust to uncertain traffic demand. Leveraging the regularity and symmetry inherent in LEO constellations, we analyze traffic-oblivious routing schemes that exploit this structure. We show that Valiant Load Balancing (VLB) is optimal for symmetric networks in minimizing worst-case congestion. On the topology side, we demonstrate that minimizing average shortest path length (ASPL) leads to asymptotically optimal performance as the network scales. We introduce a new class of symmetric and uniform topologies, called 2-color topologies, which outperform conventional grid-based designs in terms of worst-case congestion and ASPL. In particular, we prove that 2-color topologies admit an ASPL lower bound scaling of Θ(N3), whereas traditional grid-based topologies have an ASPL lower bound of Θ(N) for a network of N nodes. We validate these performance gains on a realistic-scale LEO constellation with practical link range constraints.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Poster: Wideband RFI Control using Digital Interferer/Jammer Extraction and Analog Subtraction.
abstract: High-power jamming/RFI in out-of-band spectrum can cause receiver nonlinearity and reduced ADC dynamic range in sensitive RF receivers. Radio frequency interference (RFI) is typically distributed in clumps across the spectrum, and signals of interest are interspaced with RFI in the frequency domain. Although analog passive filters can suppress known RFI bands, the frequency spectrum of RFI is not fixed and needs real-time reconfiguration. This work proposes an analog cancellation scheme in which clean copies of bandpass RFI components are selectively enhanced in the digital domain and applied in analog for real-time cancellation across wide bandwidths. This poster presents a reconfigurable FIR digital filter for real-time RFI cancellation implemented on an RF-SoC platform. The filter employs a polyphase systolic array matrix-vector multiplication (MVM) engine, with adaptive coefficients dynamically loaded to suppress narrowband and broadband interference. The extracted RFI signal is converted through a DAC and subtracted from the antenna input in the analog domain. For a single-tone interferer at 151.25 MHz, 34.4 dB of real-time RFI cancellation was achieved within a 1 GHz instantaneous receiver bandwidth, reducing the RFI-driven headroom requirement at the second ADC by 34.4 dB, potentially allowing increased downstream gain and improved utilization of the ADC dynamic range.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: OAM-Enabled Multi-User Uplink for Sub-THz Networks.
abstract: The sub-THz frequency band offers significant potential to increase wireless capacity, providing the capability to accommodate growing network demands. Multi-user uplink further improves spectral efficiency, enabling high-throughput communication from multiple users to a common access point. In this work, we propose Multiuser OAM Uplink for Sub-THz (MOUST), a sub-THz multi-user communication framework that leverages orbital-angular-momentum (OAM) multiplexing to enable high-rate communications. To adapt orthogonal, broadside OAM systems for multi-user reception, we perform receive beam-steering for each user and embed each singleuser phase profile into a multi-user receive aperture. We validate the proposed approach using two sub-THz experimental testbeds: one to characterize the amplitude and phase profiles across a wide bandwidth, and another to evaluate achievable data rates and multiuser gains. From these results, we perform extensive analysis and observe an average 1.75x multi-user sum-rate gain compared to single-user transmission for two users. This provides insight into practical design trade-offs and quantifies the multi-user multiplexing capabilities of MOUST.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: BrewSense: A Mobile Water Quality Monitoring Platform using Laser Reflection near Brewster Angle.
abstract: BrewSense is a mobile water-quality monitoring platform for realtime, large-scale detection of inland water pollution beyond the reach of grab sampling and remote sensing, whose alternatives are invasive, expensive, or limited to narrow classes of solutes and controlled environments. BrewSense leverages laser reflection near Brewster's angle to remotely infer the refractive index of surface water, which varies approximately linearly with the concentration of both ionic and organic solutes. It combines a beam-splitter and orthogonal-polarizer front-end that strongly suppresses ambient light, synchronized electrodynamic indexers with magnetic angle sensing, and hierarchical angular sampling, Gaussian spot filtering, and derivative-based Brewster-angle fitting that stabilize measurements under platform motion, waves, turbidity, and temperature variations. Implemented on a UAV, BrewSense operates at meter-scale standoff distances and achieves sub-10-4 refractive-index resolution under controlled conditions. Controlled and real-lake-water tank experiments evaluate inorganic salts (NaCl, NH4Cl) and organic solutes (glucose, urea), and a UAV deployment validates end-to-end operation in a NaCl-dominated field setting. BrewSense achieves up to 3.2× lower error than prior UWB and vibration-based systems and an approximately 8% mean relative concentration-estimation error across 20 UAV field sites.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Online Joint Pricing and Scheduling in Distributed Networked Platforms.
abstract: In distributed networked platforms, such as geographically distributed data centers and electric vehicle charging networks, there are multiple resource providers that can serve user requests arriving sequentially over time. In this paper, we study an online posted pricing problem jointly with scheduling in distributed networked platforms. In such systems, user requests arrive sequentially over time, and each request (if accepted) can be served by one of multiple resource providers. Rather than centrally assigning a provider, the platform posts prices together with corresponding scheduling decisions for all providers, and each user independently selects one option or leaves based on the posted prices and its private valuation. As demand increases, posted pricing and scheduling act as complementary mechanisms for regulating system usage. However, designing effective online posted pricing policies is challenging because of uncertainty in arrivals and the intertemporal coupling across requests, where current pricing decisions affect future feasibility and performance. We propose a class of parameterized threshold-based posted pricing policies that enable tractable online decision-making with provable performance guarantees. We identify a sufficient condition that ensures feasibility and supports competitive analysis, which in turn characterizes a structured policy design space. Building on this structure, we develop a learning-based approach to improve empirical performance under realistic demand patterns. We evaluate our approach on the problem of pricing and scheduling in electric vehicle charging stations using real-world charging traces, and demonstrate that the empirical performance of our algorithm outperforms other benchmark algorithms.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Rethinking Passive RIS at Sub-6 GHz: A Reality Check on Practical Gains.
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) promise low-power link enhancement through programmable reflections, yet their value at sub-6 GHz, where direct paths and rich multipath already exist, remains unclear. We combine Sionna ray tracing with indoor and outdoor over-the-air measurements of a 2 × 2 MIMO-OFDM system using a 144-element dual-polarized, near-passive prototype with a 25λ2 aperture and approximately 175 mW of control-plane power. Even at radiative-near-field separations favorable to the cascaded link budget, gains remain highly conditional: directional illumination improves the weaker mode by up to 11 dB indoors over no reflector, but primarily strengthens the dominant mode by 6-8 dB outdoors over a matched metal reflector. Under low-gain monopole illumination, the RIS does not consistently improve the weaker mode and can degrade it by up to about 5 dB. Thus, compact near-passive RIS is not broadly beneficial; its gains depend critically on the incident power at the RIS and the propagation environment.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Semantic-Aware Scheduling for Task-Oriented Communication by Mitigating Congestion in Emergency Networks.
abstract: Modern communication systems have fundamentally relied on bit-level perfect transmission, which becomes critically inefficient in resource-constrained disaster scenarios where bandwidth is scarce and timely information is paramount. The convergence of sensing, artificial intelligence, and communication is emerging as a key paradigm for next-generation networks, where semantic communication, transmitting the contextual meaning of data rather than raw bits, offers a promising solution. However, existing semantic approaches lack the integration of emergency-critical semantic extraction from visual sensors with semantic-aware network resource allocation. This paper bridges this gap by proposing a novel end-to-end semantic communication framework for congested emergency networks. We develop a task-oriented image captioning pipeline that fine-tunes a BLIP model on a custom-built dataset annotated with emergency-critical captions to convert sensed images into concise, actionable textual descriptions. Furthermore, we design a suite of semantic-aware MAC schedulers (specifically, DRR-Sorted, DRR-Boosted, DRR-Hybrid, and PF-Priority) that utilize content-derived priority tags to intelligently allocate network resources and mitigate congestion. Integrated into an OMNeT++/Simu5G simulation of a 5G mmWave network with a constrained backhaul, our framework delivers emergency information over 98% faster than traditional image transmission. This represents a paradigm shift from multi-second delays to near-instantaneous delivery of life-saving intelligence for first responders, demonstrating the practical benefits of tightly integrated sensing, AI, and communication pipelines.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Physics-Informed Kernelized Thompson Sampling for Beam Management in Millimeter-Wave Systems.
abstract: Maintaining connectivity in directional millimeter-wave communications requires frequent beam probing and realignment, incurring substantial overhead. We address this challenge by formulating beam tracking as a kernelized multi-armed bandit over the two-dimensional beam-angle domain. We propose GP-TSAF, a Gaussian process Thompson sampling algorithm with a physics-informed array-factor (AF) kernel. Derived directly from the known array geometry and beam codebook, the AF kernel captures beam-pattern overlap, including sidelobe interactions and null-induced decorrelation, without learning the beam-correlation structure from data. This allows each received signal strength (RSS) observation to update the posterior over the full codebook, enabling data-efficient tracking under limited measurements. To improve robustness under mobility, we further introduce adaptive correlation scaling, which weakens cross-beam smoothing as the prediction error increases without requiring an explicit mobility model. For a stationary fixed-kernel variant, we establish a cumulative-regret bound whose kernel-dependent complexity is characterized by the AF-kernel spectrum. Evaluation on 30 GHz simulation datasets with 32- and 64-beam codebooks and a 28 GHz over-the-air dataset with a 28-beam codebook shows that GP-TSAF achieves lower mean oracle gap and cumulative regret than several baselines.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Continuous Passive Target Tracking over Intermittent and Narrow Sensing Beams in 6G Networks.
abstract: 6G networks promise an advanced infrastructure for high-precision passive sensing and tracking, particularly in emerging sectors like Low-Altitude Economy (LAE) and Internet of Vehicles. However, realizing passive sensing in 6G remains challenging due to its unique signal characteristics, especially the extreme directionality of narrow beams and the intermittent availability of sensing resources, which are subordinated to the primary communication traffic. In this paper, we propose SPOT, a novel passive beam tracking framework that achieves continuous, high-precision tracking using only temporally sparse sensing slots. We employ an Interacting Multiple Model combined with an Extended Kalman Filter (IMM-EKF) to robustly predict non-linear target dynamics. We further develop a beam selection strategy that maximizes Fisher information gain to minimize tracking uncertainty, integrated with an opportunistic exploration mechanism to detect emerging targets. To reduce computation complexity, we introduce a lightweight approximation of the Posterior Cramér-Rao Lower Bound. Extensive evaluations using both simulations and real-world datasets demonstrate that SPOT significantly outperforms existing baselines, achieving a detection rate near 100% and an average tracking error below 1 meter, even in multi-target scenarios with highly sparse temporal updates.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Serving Chain-structured Jobs with Large Memory Footprints with Application to Large Foundation Model Serving.
abstract: As a current trend in Artificial Intelligence (AI), large foundation models are increasingly employed as the core of AI services. However, even after training, serving such models at scale remains a challenging task due to their heavy resource footprints, particularly in terms of GPU memory. While recent works revealed unique characteristics of systems serving foundation models that distinguish them from traditional distributed computing systems, there is still a lack of fundamental understanding of the underlying system management problems. This work aims at addressing this gap by extracting a novel problem of “server chain composition” via block placement and cache allocation for serving chain-structured jobs with large memory footprints, which models a fundamental problem in serving large foundation models through pipeline parallelism. After showing the NP-hardness of the optimal solution, the focus is turned to developing scalable algorithms with guaranteed performance under state-of-the-art load balancing. Application of the proposed solution to a distributed large language model (LLM) serving system shows significant reduction of response times compared to state-of-the-art solutions.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Shear: Goal-Oriented Anomaly Detection on Compressed Time Series via Semantic Transition Graph.
abstract: Sensor data in IoT systems are commonly compressed to meet resource constraints, yet anomaly detection directly on compressed data remains largely unexplored. This challenge is particularly evident for recurrent anomalies, which commonly appear as repeated abnormal patterns in long-running IoT streams. Existing approaches often become cumbersome or expensive since they decouple compression from analytics, requiring detection to reprocess full raw data, while supervised deep learning alternatives further demand labels or incur computational overhead unsuitable for edge deployment. In this paper, we propose Shear, a goal-oriented unsupervised method via Semantic Transition Graph (STG) induced directly from compressed time series. The STG organizes compressed representation as semantic states and encodes their temporal transitions, so that recurrent anomaly patterns are identified through unlikely state transition chains without decompression or neural network inference. Experiments on public datasets show that Shear achieves better detection performance than state-of-the-art approaches, while running 3.9× to 11.2× faster than subsequence-oriented methods and up to 2219× faster than deep learning baselines, with substantially reduced storage and memory footprint.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Resource-Constrained Semantic-Aware Remote Estimation with Overlapping Sensor Coverage.
abstract: We study semantic-aware remote estimation of multiple finite-state Markov sources observed by K sensors with overlapping coverage. The sensors share a time-division multiple-access uplink and differ in transmission reliability, delivery delay, and transmission budget. In each slot, the scheduler jointly selects a source and one of its monitoring sensors, or remains idle, to minimize the long-run average cost of actuation error subject to global and per-sensor transmission-frequency constraints. We formulate this problem as a finite average-cost constrained Markov decision process. We show that the transmission resource functions have rank at most K. Consequently, the Lagrangian depends only on K effective transmission costs, and an optimal constrained solution can be represented using at most K +1 deterministic policy-recurrent-class components. We further characterize the piecewise-affine concave Lagrangian value function and derive projected dual subgradient ascent over an explicitly bounded multiplier set. Numerical results illustrate the value-function structure, the need for policy randomization in a representative instance, and the interaction between global and per-sensor transmission budgets.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Wait to be Fresh: Optimal Sampling for Asymmetric Multi-Source Status Updates under Probabilistic Scheduling.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the exact age-optimal sampling policy for an asymmetric multi-source status update system operating under a probabilistic scheduler. Our objective is to minimize the long-term average weighted AoI when transmitting packets of varying importance over asymmetric channels with distinct random delay distributions, for any given probabilistic scheduler. We rigorously prove that the optimal sampling policy follows a strict threshold structure, providing the first exact closed-form system of equations to determine these optimal thresholds for asymmetric sources. Crucially, our theoretical analysis reveals that the relative sizing of these thresholds is strictly governed by the ratio of a source's weight to its scheduling probability, completely decoupled from highly asymmetric channel delay distributions. Numerical evaluations demonstrate that our proposed policy consistently outperforms existing baseline schemes, particularly under extreme asymmetric network conditions.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Your Palm Is in My Hand: Palm-Vein Biometric Spoofing via Electromagnetic Side Channel.
abstract: As a biometric modality, palm-vein authentication has seen growing adoption in recent years and is becoming prevalent in wallet-free payments and critical access-control applications. Although palm-vein patterns are widely regarded as nearly impossible to forge or steal, our study reveals that electromagnetic emanations induced during sensor operation can leak information correlated with a user's palm-vein characteristics, enabling attackers to reconstruct palm-vein images and spoof authentication systems. In this paper, we present PVSpy, a novel attack framework that demonstrates the feasibility of this attack. Specifically, PVSpy passively captures electromagnetic emanations radiated from palm-vein sensors, extracts features that map the captured signals to palm-vein images, and exploits diffusion models for biometric reconstructions to spoof palm-vein authentication devices. We extensively evaluate PVSpy on five commercial devices, and the recovered vein patterns exhibit a promising level of similarity. In addition, we conduct 30 end-to-end spoofing attacks against these commercial-off-the-shelf devices with different types of palm-vein sensors, and PVSpy achieves 26.7% (top-1) and 63.3% (top-3) success rates.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: From Prediction to Decision: Dynamic Maintenance Scheduling in Industrial Edge Computing via Federated DRL.
abstract: In industrial edge computing, numerous devices must operate continuously to support time-critical services. Their degradation can lead to localized failures and reduce overall system uptime, making proactive maintenance necessary. Existing data-driven maintenance methods typically predict device health or remaining useful life using deep learning models and then trigger maintenance through predefined thresholds and heuristic rules. However, this open-loop paradigm cannot dynamically adapt its decisions to evolving conditions and struggles to scale maintenance intelligence across distributed edge sites, especially under data privacy constraints. This paper transitions from prediction to decision by reformulating maintenance scheduling as a closed-loop sequential decision-making problem. Specifically, we formulate a Long-Term Operational Cost Minimization (LTOCM) problem over three device operational modes to directly capture the trade-off between failure loss and maintenance cost. Based on LTOCM, we construct a Markov decision process with a cost-based reward and further introduce a degradation-aware reward to provide informative learning signals for maintenance timing. We then propose FDDM, a federated deep reinforcement learning scheme in which edge agents learn closed-loop maintenance policies locally and collaboratively improve them across distributed industrial edge sites without sharing raw operational data. Momentum-based global aggregation is further incorporated to stabilize federated policy learning. Extensive experiments on the NASA C-MAPSS dataset across multiple fault scenarios show that FDDM achieves near-optimal operational cost and faster convergence than representative baselines. Ablation and non-IID evaluations validate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed design.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Poster: When Safer AI Makes the System Less Safe: Inference Reuse and Systemic Risk in Networked Autonomy.
abstract: Network-assisted inference can improve the decisions of autonomous agents, while reusing inference results can avoid repeated computation. However, when multiple agents reuse the same inference result, their failures become more coupled. We show that beyond a simple threshold, simultaneous failure can become more likely even though every agent is individually more accurate. We then characterize when the resource savings from reuse justify this added shared-failure risk.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Demo: A Hybrid-Manufactured 3D-Printed Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface.
abstract: Practical research on Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces and H-MIMO surfaces requires low-cost, full-scale prototypes for testing their performance in real-world wireless links. However, conventional prototypes typically use expensive radio-frequency (RF) components and precisely manufactured printed circuit boards (PCBs) with stable dielectric properties to achieve a wide operating band and low reflection loss. Additive manufacturing (AM), or 3D printing, offers an attractive alternative by enabling rapid fabrication of low-cost RIS structures with geometries that are difficult to create using conventional PCB manufacturing techniques. This demo presents the first hybrid 3D-printed surface, which combines an inexpensive, standard FR-4 PCB carrying the control circuit with low-cost 3D-printed layers that provide a wide operating bandwidth. The demonstration includes OFDM transmission over the 4.6-5.35 GHz frequency range with a protective 3D-printed radome installed. In the geometry evaluated during the demo, the surface provides a received-power gain of up to 24 dB relative to the scenario without tge surface. The results show that hybrid fabrication based on low-cost AM and PCB technologies can be used to construct practical RIS testbeds for experimental wireless research.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: FSMA: Scaling LoRa Satellite IoT with Link-aware Multiple Access.
abstract: Direct-to-satellite LoRa is rapidly becoming infrastructure for global IoT, but it faces a fundamental medium access control (MAC) bottleneck: a satellite's large footprint causes thousands of devices to collide on the same channel, while its motion induces rapid link variations, making link-unaware transmissions a persistent source of wasted airtime. These challenges demand random access solutions without requiring synchronization, handshakes, or an additional channel. However, ALOHA leaves collisions uncoordinated, and carrier sensing fails because devices across a footprint cannot hear each other. We propose Free Signal Multiple Access (FSMA), a gateway-controlled MAC protocol that works like a traffic light: the gateway sends a single LoRa upchirp (FreeChirp) only while the channel is idle, confining contention to a short sensing window, and at a lower spreading factor than the node uplink, implicitly deferring weak-link nodes through channel reciprocity, all without handshakes or hardware modifications. Hardware experiments with up to 25 off-the-shelf LoRa nodes and static and drone-mounted gateways demonstrate 2× higher throughput and 2.5-5× better packet reception ratio. Simulations with real satellite trajectories confirm scalability to 5000 devices per satellite pass, with up to 6.4× lower energy per successful packet.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: TSDM: A Scheduling Policy for Joint Throughput-AoI Optimization in Multichannel Wireless Networks.
abstract: Optimizing for both low Age of Information (AoI) and high throughput is critical for remote sensing applications that rely on multichannel wireless networks. However, jointly optimizing these two metrics is an analytically challenging problem, particularly in systems with heterogeneous and unreliable channels. To address this challenge, we propose TSDM, a Two-Stage Deficit Matching scheduling framework. TSDM is based on a second-order approach that characterizes the performance of each data flow by its mean and temporal variance. In the first stage, TSDM translates the highlevel utility maximization objective into a concrete set of target mean and temporal variance statistics for transmissions over each node-channel pair. In the second stage, a low-complexity Weighted Matching Deficit (WMD) rule performs real-time channel assignment. We theoretically prove that TSDM achieves the desired mean and temporal variance for each flow. Furthermore, we conduct extensive simulations on two open problems in joint throughput-AoI optimization. In both cases, TSDM significantly outperforms existing scheduling policies.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Fresh Enough to Decide: Age of Intelligence for Cost-Aware Model Synchronization in Dynamic IoT Systems.
abstract: Resource-constrained IoT devices cache learned models for realtime decisions, but frequent updates incur substantial bandwidth, energy, and service overhead. Because decision-relevant model differences need not grow with elapsed time, we define Age of Intelligence (AoInt) as a model-version-relative, client-specific, and action utility distortion, and formulate synchronization as a tradeoff between stale-decision regret and refresh cost. Furthermore, we develop Kullback-Leibler-aware AoInt Synchronization (KL-AoIntSync), which accumulates output-distribution changes using client-specific unlabeled probes, whereas Parameter-aware AoInt Synchronization (Param-AoIntSync) uses a server-broadcast scalar parameter change. Then, we establish pathwise guarantees with fixed client distributions, action sets, and utilities. The numerical results show that calibrated Param-AoIntSync reduces joint synchronization cost by 6.15% relative to an Instant-Parameters policy while performing comparably to KL-AoIntSync.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Demo: On-Device Agent for Personalized and Efficient Mobile Network Configuration.
abstract: As mobile devices increasingly operate across heterogeneous access networks and diverse usage contexts, efficient network configuration requires decisions that adapt to both dynamic network conditions and individual user preferences. We demonstrate an on-device communication agent that transforms historical user network-switching behavior into personalized configuration rules. An on-device Large language model (LLM) analyzes switching records offline and generates condition-action rules capturing recurring user preferences. During real-time use, the agent retrieves matched rules locally and executes the corresponding network configuration after user confirmation, without invoking the LLM. Attendees will choose a prepared behavior trace, inspect the rule generated on the phone, and recreate its triggering context to observe an immediate network switch. The demonstration shows how separating deliberation from execution makes personalized mobile network configuration both interpretable and responsive while keeping user data and inference on the device.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: WISEMap: Simultaneous Infrastructure and Layout Mapping via Enterprise Wi-Fi.
abstract: Environment-aware capabilities have been envisioned to enhance Wi-Fi networks in communication, localization, and sensing. However, existing environment-aware approaches often assume prior knowledge of infrastructure (AP orientations and locations) and environment maps, limiting their applicability in real-world deployments. We present WISEMap, a framework that simultaneously reconstructs infrastructure and indoor layout via enterprise Wi-Fi, without prior information. The core challenge lies in the tight coupling between the two tasks: layout reconstruction demands precise infrastructure mapping, which in turn requires accurate mapping of the layout. WISEMap addresses this challenge by alternately optimizing the two tasks and progressively refining their estimates. Real-world evaluations show that WISEMap not only accomplishes both tasks simultaneously but also delivers substantially higher accuracy than the baselines designed for each task, reducing layout reconstruction error by 43-77% and the average AP and user localization errors by 70% and 39%, respectively.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Joint Optimizing Federated Learning and Unlearning over Wireless Networks.
abstract: In this paper, a communication and energy-efficient federated learning (FL) and unlearning (FU) co-designed framework is proposed. In the considered model, multiple edge devices collaboratively train a model. Users are allowed to quit the FL training and remove their data impacts on the trained model. Hence, an FU training is performed after the FL training. To reduce the energy and time consumption of FU, the users are grouped into multiple clusters such that the users in a group will retrain a deep learning model when the users in the group request to quit the FL training. The base station (BS) needs to determine the number of clusters, the users in each cluster, and the resource block (RB) allocated to each user, according to the probability that each user requests to quit the FL, data distribution, wireless channel conditions, and time and energy constraints. This problem is formulated as an optimization problem whose goal is to minimize the expected loss by determining the number of clusters, user cluster assignment, and RB allocations. This problem is challenging to solve since 1) the BS cannot predict which users will request data deletion in advance and 2) no explicit equation exists to capture the relationship between the number of clusters, user cluster assignment, and the expected FU loss. To solve the formulated problem, we first analyze the convergence rate of FU to build an explicit relationship among the FU training loss, the number of clusters, and the users in each cluster. Based on this relationship, the original problem is simplified to a mixed-integer optimization problem which can be divided into the user cluster assignment and the RB allocation optimization subproblems. These two problems are alternately solved by the designed Dinkelbach's method and the fast iterative shrinkage-thresholding algorithm (Dinkelbach-FISTA) and the standard Hungarian algorithm. Simulation results show that our method improves classification accuracy by up to 11.1% and achieves up to 3× faster convergence compared to gradient-based and ISTA-based methods.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Over-the-Air Federated Learning in Heterogeneous Mobile Wireless Networks.
abstract: Over-the-air computation has emerged as a scalable and efficient solution for deploying federated learning algorithms in wireless networks by exploiting waveform superposition for simultaneous model aggregation. Most existing work struggles with heterogeneous fading channels. These approaches either enforce unbiased updates from all devices or allow partial device contributions, requiring careful tuning of the convergence bound to mitigate bias under specific fading models. However, the former significantly amplifies receiver noise due to the weakest channel, whereas the latter is sensitive to fading model mismatch and converges only to a biased objective. To tackle these challenges, we propose FedOAG, which employs algorithmic components to automatically satisfy energy constraints via gradient normalization and evenly mix devices' updates through implicit gossiping. Importantly, FedOAG does not require transmission from all devices, nor does it rely on a specific fading model or knowledge of time-varying statistical channel distributions. We show that FedOAG converges to a stationary point of an unbiased non-convex objective at the best possible rate O(1/T) for any stochastic first-order method. We corroborate our analysis with numerical experiments over dynamic wireless conditions on real-world datasets.

title: ECO-COMM: An Ultra Low-Latency Event Camera based Optical Communication System.
abstract: Ultra-low-latency communication is critical for emerging applications such as XR, real-time control, and distributed sensing. We present ECO-COMM, an event-camera-based optical communication system for ultra-low-latency device association and lightweight information exchange. By exploiting the asynchronous sensing and microsecond-level temporal resolution of event cameras, ECO-COMM captures high-frequency optical signals without frame-based acquisition delays. We identify and analyze key hardware-induced challenges in event-camera communication, including timestamp inconsistency, readout contention, trailing effects, and the inevitable refractory period, and develop hardware-aware mitigation techniques to address them. Focusing on a single transmitter-receiver optical link, ECO-COMM establishes the feasibility of practical ultra-low-latency event-camera communication using commercially available hardware. A prototype implementation using an eight-LED transmitter and an off-the-shelf event camera achieves device association within 15 μs, symbol latency as low as 100 μs, and end-to-end latency below 8 ms for 32-byte payloads at a 0.1% bit error rate. Overall, ECO-COMM establishes a practical and complementary communication paradigm for ultra-low-latency systems.

title: Error Tolerant Neural Media Codecs for 6G AI-on-RAN.
abstract: Running neural media codecs on the RAN enables bandwidth-efficient and low-latency delivery in the emerging AI on radio access network (AI-on-RAN) paradigm. However, both conventional and neural codecs, e.g., JPEG and vector-quantized variational autoencoder (VQ-VAE), may degrade severely under packet loss and residual bit errors. While entropy coding in conventional codecs may cause extensive error propagation, the independently decodable discrete latents of neural codecs provide an opportunity to design codec-level error tolerance. This paper introduces EMA-SVTC, a unified quantization framework for error-prone 6G AI-on-RAN systems that combines exponential moving average (EMA) codebook updates with a semantically-adjacent vector transition constraint (SVTC). The constraint shapes the topological structure of the latent space by encouraging neighboring latent indices to correspond to semantically similar representations, thereby limiting the distortion caused by bit errors within individual latents while retaining independent decoding across latents and avoiding cross-latent error propagation. We apply the proposed framework to speech and image codecs based on finite scalar quantization (FSQ) and VQ-VAE, respectively. Experiments over error-prone wireless channels show that, at a bit error rate of 10-2, the proposed speech codec raises the perceptual evaluation of speech quality (PESQ) score from 1.44 for the conventional super-FSQ baseline to 2.51 with a 21× smaller model and to 2.97 at equal model size, corresponding to relative gains of 74% and 106%, while the proposed image codec raises the structural similarity index measure (SSIM) from 0.73 to 0.89 at the same bit error rate and preserves 0.86 at 2% BER, where JPEG has already collapsed. The proposed designs achieve comparable media quality at lower SNRs, reducing the need for nearly error-free wireless transport without introducing additional parity bits.

title: Poster: Steady-State Approximation Error of Heterogeneous Mean-Field Models.
abstract: Mean-field models provide tractable approximations for large-scale stochastic systems by replacing stochastic interactions among many agents with deterministic dynamics. They have been widely used in epidemic models, queueing and load-balancing systems, communication networks, and interacting particle systems. For homogeneous systems, [3] established an O (1/M) bound on the steady-state mean-square approximation error for a broad class of mean-field models, where M is the number of agents. The analysis is based on Stein's method [2] and shows that exponential stability of the mean-field dynamics plays a central role in determining the approximation error. Many systems in practice are inherently heterogeneous, such as an epidemic model with heterogeneous infection rates. For heterogeneous mean-field models, finite-time approximation results have been established in [1], which characterize the approximation error of the marginal state distribution of individual agents over a finite time horizon. This is an extended abstract of the arXiv paper [4], which studies steady-state approximation errors. We establish an O (1/ M ) bound on the steady-state mean-square error between the occupancy measure of the M -agent system and the corresponding mean-field equilibrium. The analysis extends Stein's method for homogeneous mean-field models and reveals a fundamental difference between homogeneous and heterogeneous systems. While stability of the mean-field dynamics is sufficient in the homogeneous setting, heterogeneous systems further require uniform robustness of the occupancy dynamics with respect to perturbations of the initial condition. In general, finite-time convergence does not imply convergence of stationary distributions, and establishing steady-state convergence requires additional arguments related to stability and interchange of limits. Therefore, a finite-time approximation bound does not directly apply to steady-state approximation.

title: Queue-Stable Online Learning: Bilinear Bandits for Semantic Codecs in NTNs.
abstract: On a narrowband non-terrestrial network (NTN) link, speech codec selection affects both reconstruction quality and the payload awaiting transmission. Each codec profile specifies bitrate, transmit power, codebook size, and recurrent-layer count. First transmissions and retransmissions share the payload capacity granted by the modem. We present the Lyapunov Bilinear Upper Confidence Bound scheduler, LyBUCB, which learns profile quality from selected-action feedback and combines its confidence score with the unsent payload queue and a virtual queue that accumulates distortion-budget excess. A transport ledger separately records unsent payload, retransmissions, unacknowledged payload, and unique acknowledgments. We bound finite-horizon decision error relative to a drift-plus-penalty oracle evaluated on the same predecision state. Under independent and identically distributed external observations and strict feasibility, exact search yields queue and online-score bounds; ranking with the preceding interference observation adds an approximation term. Tiantong measurements and closed-loop tests with recorded traces show higher session speech quality than five baselines within the preset queue and distortion limits. The measured 95th-percentile observation-to-encoder and scheduler latencies, together with the maximum score-return interval, are below the 500-ms slot duration.

title: Ripple: Coordination-Free Message Scheduling for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows at the IoT Edge.
abstract: Distributed intelligence in IoT and edge systems increasingly runs as agentic AI: production large language model (LLM) applications execute as workflows—directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) of agents and tools that exchange prompts, retrieved context, and tool outputs across end devices, edge servers, and the cloud. When many such workflows share a capacity-limited link, such as an edge gateway uplink or a regional aggregation point, that link rather than the GPU gates the communication phase, and a message that unblocks an idle agent may wait behind an unrelated bulk transfer. A dependency-aware link scheduler can mitigate this, but a scheduler that ranks messages by whole-workflow remaining work and downstream critical path requires a global, continuously updated view of every concurrent workflow, that is, a central coordinator that heterogeneous and dynamic IoT edge deployments typically lack. This paper presents Ripple, a coordination-free link scheduler in which each agent ranks only its own outgoing messages, using a local rule that prioritizes downstream criticality per unit transmission cost and applies an age credit to curb long waits. The required downstream-criticality signal is a bounded scalar initialized with the source's task descriptor, so no runtime node maintains the global graph. In an event-driven, flow-level evaluation on a shared 100 Mbps link with heavy-tailed messages (median 419 KB, 99th-percentile about 30 MB) and four DAG shapes, network waiting accounts for 46% of the mean workflow completion time (WCT) under fair sharing at offered load ρ=0.88. Ripple reduces mean and 99th-percentile WCT by 24% and 38% relative to fair sharing, and attains 9% lower mean and 27% lower tail WCT than a global-view reference heuristic while using no global state. A knowledge-horizon analysis shows that performance saturates at a one-hop view, and an ablation finds that message size and age drive most of the aggregate gain. The results use an idealized flow-level priority model; a DSCP/eBPF realization that needs no coordinator and no change to the LLM runtime is proposed but not yet evaluated.

title: Poster: ProbeGuard, Budgeted Active Probing for Safe LLM Service Recomposition under Silent Semantic Drift.
abstract: Under silent semantic drift, an upgraded edge-cloud service stays schema-compatible but changes a unit, precondition, or state transition, invalidating LLM-orchestrated compositions. ProbeGuard treats candidate behaviors as a version space and spends a small budget of safe probes to discriminate them; owner-protected executable clauses cannot be weakened by an LLM, and a service is cleared only when all evidence-compatible hypotheses agree. In 252 controlled episodes, hybrid hypothesis generation recovers 94.8% of drifted behaviors, and ProbeGuard automates 98.4% of decisions correctly while cutting harmful clearance from 5.3% to 2.7% and latency from 0.94 to 0.56 s versus the strongest deployable baseline.

title: Restless Bandits with Individual Penalty Constraints: Near-Optimal Indices and Deep Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: This paper investigates the Restless Multi-Armed Bandit (RMAB) framework under individual penalty constraints to address resource allocation challenges in dynamic wireless networked environments. Unlike conventional RMAB models, our model allows each user (arm) to have distinct and stringent performance constraints, such as energy limits, activation limits, or age of information minimums, enabling the capture of diverse objectives including fairness and efficiency. To find the optimal resource allocation policy, we propose a new Penalty-Optimal Whittle (POW) index policy. The POW index of an user only depends on the user's transition kernel and penalty constraints, and remains invariable to system-wide features such as the number of users present and the amount of resource available. This makes it computationally tractable to calculate the POW indices offline without any need for online adaptation. Moreover, we theoretically prove that the POW index policy is asymptotically optimal while satisfying all individual penalty constraints. We also introduce a deep reinforcement learning algorithm to efficiently learn the POW index on the fly. Simulation results across various applications and system configurations further demonstrate that the POW index policy not only has near-optimal performance but also significantly outperforms other existing policies.

title: Poster: Open RAN-Enabled Transparent Proxies for High Throughput and Low Latency.
abstract: Driven by delayed end-to-end feedback, TCP congestion control cannot promptly track the fast-changing capacity of cellular wireless links, limiting its ability to simultaneously deliver high throughput and low latency. Performance-enhancing proxies (PEPs) were proposed to shorten the control loop by generating proactive feedback near the wireless bottleneck, but their limited network visibility and poor deployability have hindered widespread adoption. Emerging open RAN (O-RAN) architectures reopen the design space for PEPs by exposing RAN observability and supporting programmable edge infrastructure. This poster presents O-Proxy, a transparent PEP built on O-RAN. Using observations of RLC-layer queue length and saturation rate, O-Proxy applies a model-free adaptive control scheme to adjust the rwnd field in ACKs, thereby keeping the RAN queue near an operating point that balances low latency and high throughput. Compared with the strongest middlebox baseline, O-Proxy reduces median latency by 50%.

title: Skynet: Workflow-Level Anomaly Detection for Agentic AI via Semantic and Structural Modeling.
abstract: Agentic AI systems execute complex tasks through long-horizon workflows of planning, tool use, and multi-agent coordination. Task failures in these systems often originate from a single step, such as an injected prompt or a flawed plan, and are then amplified through downstream dependencies as the corrupted step propagates across many subsequent agents and tool calls. Existing defenses either target a specific class of attacks or failures, or inspect individual prompts and steps in isolation. Both leave the global dependency structure of a workflow unexamined, and miss the inconsistencies that only emerge when the execution is viewed as a whole. We argue that anomaly detection for agentic AI must reason at the workflow level, where global execution structure exposes signals that local checks cannot see. We present Skynet, a principled workflow-level anomaly detection framework that turns observed multi-agent execution into directed workflow graphs and scores them against learned benign behavior. Skynet jointly models the semantic execution context and the structural organization of inter-agent delegation, tool invocation, and data-flow dependencies, and trains only on benign workflows. Because training never sees attacks or failures, this design naturally extends to zero-day detection: any execution that violates benign workflow regularities surfaces as off-manifold geometry under a single decision rule. We evaluate Skynet on three public agentic safety and failure benchmarks. It sustains high recall together with a sub-1% false positive rate, with per-workflow and per-step latencies low enough for online monitoring of agentic AI runtimes.

title: MOSAIC: Efficient Collaborative Inference for Multi-Modal Large Language Models with Distributed Edge Computing.
abstract: Multi-modal large language models (MLLMs) enable natural language reasoning over heterogeneous sensory data, appealing to many edge AI scenarios, yet their deployment faces competing demands on latency, energy, and quality. We present MOSAIC, which adopts a component-level decomposition and distributed deployment paradigm for efficient MLLM inference at the edge, realizing three core ideas: parallel encoding, token pruning, and device-server collaboration. Specifically, for the offline stage, modality-specific encoders distilled from a unified foundation model are co-deployed with Q-Former projection on edge devices for parallel encoding, while LoRA instruction fine-tuning adapts the frozen LLM backbone to downstream tasks. For the online stage, we formulate a multi-objective optimization over latency and energy that jointly tunes token budgets, device frequencies, and quantization precision under long-term semantic accuracy constraints, achieving dynamic token pruning and device-server collaboration. We leverage Lagrangian relaxation to decompose the original problem into tractable per-slot subproblems and design an online algorithm with provable near-optimal performance and guaranteed constraint satisfaction. We implement a realistic testbed for extensive performance evaluation, which demonstrates that MOSAIC reduces latency by up to 49.8% and energy by up to 65.1% over advanced baselines while maintaining high semantic accuracy.

title: Lightweight Approximate Nearest Neighbors Based Sparse Attention Transformer for NetBIOS Attack Detection in IoT Networks.
abstract: As IoT devices grow in number, NetBIOS-based DDoS attacks have become a bigger problem. These attacks can damage the speed and stability of the network. Many deep learning models use attention to improve performance. But standard attention has high complexity. That makes it too heavy for realtime use on IoT devices. In this context, we proposed a sustainable transformer model based on sparse attention. This model is based on approximate nearest neighbors (ANN)-based sparse attention. This model reduces the complexity of the attention from quadratic to O(nlog n). That makes the model much faster. The proposed model includes CMA-ES, CNN, LSTM, and ANN-based sparse attention. We tested the model on the CIC-DDoS2019 dataset. It reached 99.804% accuracy, while maintaining low computational overhead, making it highly suitable for the detection of NetBIOS attacks in IoT security systems.

title: Towards Ubiquitous Backscatter Capacitive Sensing.
abstract: This paper presents CapScatter, the first sub-10μW backscatter capacitive sensor compatible with sensing capacitors in 10-1000pF, marking a step toward ubiquitous backscatter capacitive sensing. Built on three key designs, we overcome the limitation of existing sub-10μW works compatible only with sensing capacitors below 10pF. Specifically, (i) we design an excitation-driven capacitance encoding circuit, which consists of decoupled capacitance measurement and backscatter communication subcircuits, to cover the wide capacitance range; (ii) we design a power-scanning capacitance decoding algorithm, in which the reader queries the sensor multiple times at different transmitted powers, to eliminate the interference caused by the received excitation power variations; (iii) we design a collision avoidance circuit that adds only a few passive components with negligible additional power consumption, to avoid signal collision between multiple sensors. Our experiments show that CapScatter achieves a median measurement error of 2.17% and a maximum measurement error of 3.85% over a capacitance range of 10-1000pF. Meanwhile, its static power is 4.32μW, and the operating power ranges from 6.11μW to 20.51μW.

title: MEO: Mining Reliable Expert Signals for Offline Reinforcement Learning in Wireless Networks.
abstract: The operation of next-generation wireless networks increasingly hinges on Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) to optimize critical network decisions. Offline RL trains agents using accessible datasets and thus eliminates costly online interactions, rendering it particularly advantageous in dynamic wireless environments that demand low latency and high safety. However, its capability remains under-explored in wireless settings, where offline data are often limited and subject to partial observability. As a result, the learned policy fails to fully capture the informative decision patterns hidden in the dataset. To bridge this gap, we propose MEO, a framework that mines reliable expert signals from wireless datasets for offline RL deployment. MEO first identifies reliable expert samples from imperfect offline data, and then learns a structured latent representation to better distinguish expert and non-expert behaviors. Based on the representation, MEO further derives a compensable reward signal that helps offline RL algorithms more effectively exploit valuable expert knowledge. We evaluate MEO in three practical wireless network scenarios using datasets collected from real-world deployments. The results show that MEO consistently outperforms existing methods across all three scenarios. Notably, MEO can be seamlessly integrated with any offline RL algorithms, highlighting its generalizability and potential for wide adoption in wireless networks. (Code is available at https://github.com/lpzu/MEO)
